# herdr + herdr-core feature catalog

Reference catalog for the ovis-terminal design. Built by reducing three aggregated module catalogs (agg-herdr-extract-a/b/c) of the herdr TUI multiplexer and the herdr-core headless runtime (`hc`). Every catalog citation is copied verbatim from its input row; prose citations give the CAT id plus that citation. Paths are relative to the cloned repositories under `/tmp/ulw-ovis-yCJzPH/repos`.

Selection note: the mandatory-keep rule (every api, protocol, event, config, cli, persistence, security, design, limitation, instruction or client-pain row tagged agent-friendly, agent-unfriendly or client-pain) alone yields 3209 distinct citations, so the catalog exceeds the 700-1200 target; the mandatory rule was given precedence. Feature rows are kept when tagged non-neutral or when they describe externally observable behavior; neutral tui-only rows are collapsed into one summary row per module. Rows sharing a citation and tag are merged (the input rows marked "merged duplicate" were already merged upstream).

## Architecture overview

herdr is a terminal multiplexer for coding agents: a bare `herdr` probes its socket, spawns a server daemon if none is running, waits for readiness and attaches a thin TUI client (CAT-2025 `herdr/src/server/autodetect.rs:305`). The headless `herdr server` entry point loads config, binds a JSON API socket and then a separate client socket, so the server and the TUI are distinct processes (CAT-2080 `herdr/src/server/headless/bootstrap.rs:4`). Each client-socket connection is one of ClientShell (owns the herdr UI), TerminalAttach (writable direct stream) or TerminalObserve (read-only), so herdr mixes UI ownership and terminal streams on one socket (CAT-2071 `herdr/src/server/clients.rs:12`). Client and server speak a private message protocol in the protocol module, extended through an append-only EndpointControl message whose tag and payload shape are frozen (CAT-1869 `herdr/src/protocol/wire.rs:616`). The client-owned endpoint protocol is pinned at generation 1 as a compatibility floor for Local, SSH and Cloud shells, independent of the private binary protocol (CAT-1819 `herdr/src/protocol/endpoint.rs:1`). The server, not the app state, owns PTYs, parsers, detector tasks and channels in a TerminalRuntimeRegistry keyed by an opaque, server-owned TerminalId (CAT-2257 `herdr/src/terminal/runtime_registry.rs:11`). Pane emulation in the pane/terminal modules is built on libghostty, inheriting Ghostty semantics such as its modifyOtherKeys handling (CAT-1585 `herdr/src/pane/terminal.rs:1864`). The pty actor submits prompts in phases (text, delay, Enter) and blocks other input until Enter lands, so agent TUIs do not swallow a pasted submit (CAT-1902 `herdr/src/pty/actor/unix.rs:487`). Programs drive herdr through the api module: newline-delimited JSON requests `{id, method, params}` (CAT-001 `herdr/src/api/schema.rs:37`), with roughly 100 wire methods declared by one `define_operations!` macro (CAT-002 `herdr/src/api/schema.rs:45`). The cli module wraps that API: commands print the JSON response on stdout with exit 0, the error on stderr with exit 1, and parse errors exit 2 without connecting (CAT-581 `herdr/src/cli.rs:730`). herdr's detect module infers agent state by periodically matching each pane's bottom-of-buffer text against known agent output (CAT-1307 `herdr/src/detect/mod.rs:1`). Those detection rules ship as per-agent TOML files that infer brand and state from screen text, titles and progress signals (CAT-3011 `herdr/distribution/agent-detection/amp.toml:8`). The integration module installs per-agent hooks with a version constant per target (pi, claude, codex, opencode and others) (CAT-1382 `herdr/src/integration/mod.rs:38`). The persist module saves workspaces, layouts and working dirs to session.json (CAT-1634 `herdr/src/persist.rs:3`) with an atomic fsync-and-rename write (CAT-1639 `herdr/src/persist/io.rs:49`). The remote module bridges the API over SSH and advertises a `herdr-api-bridge-v1` token for capability probing (CAT-1920 `herdr/src/remote.rs:31`); machine forwarding never installs, starts or falls back to Local (CAT-2941 `herdr/skills/herdr/SKILL.md:103`). The workspace module gives every workspace a stable public id independent of display order (CAT-2420 `herdr/src/workspace.rs:178`), and config applies each top-level section independently so one bad section does not reject the rest (CAT-1241 `herdr/src/config/io.rs:542`). The ui, input and kitty_graphics modules are human chrome: bindings are direct chords or prefix-mode (CAT-1354 `herdr/src/input/keybindings.rs:8`), and graphics are emitted only for the local host terminal (CAT-1485 `herdr/src/kitty_graphics/output.rs:1`). herdr-core (`hc`) is headless: a separate holder process owns every PTY, always reads output, keeps about 1 MB of tail per terminal and restarts a crashed core (CAT-3070 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/holder.rs:1`). hc speaks JSON-RPC over a socket; a connection starts plain (one message per line) and a `hello` with `framed: true` switches it to binary frames where channel 0 carries JSON-RPC (CAT-3111 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/server.rs:129`). Framed mode uses a 9-byte header `[channel u32][kind u8][len u32]` (CAT-3166 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/wire.rs:1`) and credit-based flow control per stream (CAT-3170 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/wire.rs:13`). Status comes only from programs writing OSC 7501 records (state, kind, progress, app, title, msg) that the core stores untranslated (CAT-3122 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/status.rs:14`); the project forbids screen detection or vendor logic (CAT-3690 `herdr-core/AGENTS.md:28`). The whole hc API is generated as an OpenRPC document served by `rpc.discover` / `hc schema` (CAT-3109 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/rpc.rs:93`), and a compatibility test forces the API to only grow against the released schema (CAT-3471 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/tests/compat.rs:1`). Terminals carry a parent address, notify flag and die_with_parent, giving declared parent/child agent trees (CAT-3139 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/terminals.rs:77`); news about a child is typed into its parent as an `<hc>` note (CAT-3088 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/notes.rs:1`). Templates are Markdown files under `~/.config/herdr-core/templates` (CAT-3128 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/templates.rs:37`), and `terminal.run` sends the template body as the first message once the agent reports ready (CAT-3131 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/templates.rs:136`). Machines are addressed as `machine/t7` with one address string working across cores (CAT-3028 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/addr.rs:1`), each dialed over ssh stdio with immediate redial and backoff (CAT-3424 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/remote.rs:225`); a versioned document store (`doc.get`/`doc.set`) gives clients shared state with compare-and-swap (CAT-3229 `herdr-core/crates/herdr-core/src/api/doc.rs:16`), and the docs/schema README define the contract from Rust types (CAT-3698 `herdr-core/schema/README.md:3`).

## Agent-friendly keepers

The 40 most valuable agent-friendly designs for ovis-terminal to adopt.

1. **CAT-3028** terminal address scheme (herdr-core / src): One address string (`t7`, `name`, `machine/t7`) works locally and across machines; adopt as the ovis-terminal addressing scheme.
2. **CAT-3195** hello (herdr-core / src/api): Single handshake returning generation, version, methods and features lets clients negotiate instead of guessing.
3. **CAT-3191** feature flags (herdr-core / src/api): Explicit feature flags in hello make optional capabilities discoverable.
4. **CAT-3190** protocol generation (herdr-core / src/api): A protocol generation number with a hard `unsupported_generation` error is a clean breaking-change gate.
5. **CAT-3109** rpc.discover / hc schema (OpenRPC 1.3.2) (herdr-core / src): Machine-readable OpenRPC document from `rpc.discover` lets agents self-discover the API.
6. **CAT-3471** API only grows (released.openrpc.json gate) (herdr-core / tests): A test that diffs against the released schema enforces an API that only grows.
7. **CAT-3472** Compatibility rules: inputs widen, outputs never narrow (herdr-core / tests): Concrete compatibility rules (inputs widen, outputs never narrow) are reusable as-is.
8. **CAT-3122** OSC 7501 status record (herdr-core / src): Program-declared status via OSC 7501 replaces screen scraping with an explicit contract.
9. **CAT-3123** Status::encode (OSC 7501) (herdr-core / src): Status re-emitted on first paint so a new viewer sees state immediately.
10. **CAT-3126** status::apply (records & clear) (herdr-core / src): Root plus child status records (by id) model sub-tasks inside one terminal.
11. **CAT-3125** turn counter (herdr-core / src): A turn counter gives waiters an unambiguous "the agent finished a turn" signal.
12. **CAT-3690** Do not infer agents (herdr-core / docs): Design rule: never infer agents from the screen; ovis-terminal should adopt it verbatim.
13. **CAT-3047** event wire format (herdr-core / src): Events are typed JSON-RPC notifications with type, terminal, data and seq.
14. **CAT-3052** event seq (herdr-core / src): A global monotonic seq lets clients order events and detect gaps.
15. **CAT-3221** events.subscribe (herdr-core / src/api): Subscribe returns a snapshot then ordered events, heartbeat and missed+snapshot recovery.
16. **CAT-3229** doc.set (optimistic concurrency) (herdr-core / src/api): Optimistic-concurrency `doc.set` gives multi-agent shared state without locks.
17. **CAT-3070** holder process (herdr-core / src): A holder process that owns PTYs decouples program lifetime from the server.
18. **CAT-3071** core crash supervision (herdr-core / src): The holder restarts a crashed core with backoff, so programs survive core crashes.
19. **CAT-3120** SIGTERM = planned restart (herdr-core / src): SIGTERM as planned restart keeps programs and screens across upgrades.
20. **CAT-3377** holder/core service model on Linux (herdr-core / src/platform): Running core and holders as systemd user services survives logout and ssh disconnect.
21. **CAT-3139** parent / notify / die_with_parent / rm (herdr-core / src): Declared parent/child links with die_with_parent replace process-tree guessing.
22. **CAT-3427** $/orphaned (herdr-core / src/remote): `$/orphaned` propagates parent death across machines, queued if the line is down.
23. **CAT-3428** remote call deadline & cancel (herdr-core / src/remote): Remote calls carry deadlines and `$/cancelRequest`, so callers never hang on a lost line.
24. **CAT-3131** Core::first_message (herdr-core / src): First message is held until the agent reports ready, avoiding typing into a booting TUI.
25. **CAT-3199** templates.list (herdr-core / src/api): `templates.list` lets an orchestrator pick roles by name without knowing commands.
26. **CAT-3198** terminal.run (herdr-core / src/api): `terminal.run` starts programs or templates through one structured call.
27. **CAT-3211** terminal.wait (herdr-core / src/api): `terminal.wait` waits on declared status/exit rather than output silence.
28. **CAT-3210** last_send turn tracking (herdr-core / src/api): Send-to-turn tracking ties a later wait to the turn the caller started.
29. **CAT-3034** observe mode (herdr-core / src): Read-only observe mode works from a pipe, giving agents a safe viewer.
30. **CAT-3166** frame layout (herdr-core / src): A tiny fixed 9-byte frame header keeps the framed transport easy to implement.
31. **CAT-581** JSON request/response CLI contract (herdr / cli): Strict stdout/stderr/exit-code contract makes every CLI call scriptable.
32. **CAT-3481** state/.../docs.json with .bad quarantine (herdr-core / tests): Corrupt state files are quarantined (`.bad`) instead of blocking startup.
33. **CAT-3666** Custom machine transport (herdr-core / docs): A custom machine transport only needs to pass bytes unchanged and ask nothing.
34. **CAT-001** Request{id,method,params} (herdr / api): Simple `{id, method, params}` NDJSON requests are trivial for any language.
35. **CAT-009** ServerCapabilities flags (herdr / api): Capability flags default to false so old servers still parse; good forward-compat pattern.
36. **CAT-084** Subscription cursor pinned before setup probes (herdr / api): Pinning the event cursor before setup probes prevents losing racing events.
37. **CAT-107** Initial synthetic status event (herdr / api): An initial synthetic status event stops waiters hanging on an already-satisfied state.
38. **CAT-1819** Endpoint stable compatibility contract (herdr / protocol): Explicit endpoint compatibility contract: new JSON fields must be optional/defaulted.
39. **CAT-1903** Submission blocks other user data until Enter done (herdr / pty): Submissions block interleaving input until Enter lands, so prompts are atomic.
40. **CAT-2255** TerminalId opaque id (herdr / terminal): Opaque server-owned terminal ids that callers must not derive from layout.

## Agent-unfriendly exclusions

All 523 agent-unfriendly catalog rows, grouped by theme. The reason is the input row's "why this tag", i.e. why ovis-terminal should not copy it.

### Brand detection (71)

- CAT-066 IntegrationTarget brand list: Agent brand detection hard-coded; new agents need a code change
- CAT-144 AppEvent::AgentProcessDetected: Agent identity is guessed from process detection (brand detection).
- CAT-145 AppEvent::CodexPromptObserved: Screen-scraped Codex prompt heuristic.
- CAT-203 Agent liveness verified by foreground process: Agent identity depends on process-name detection (brand detection) rather than a registration.
- CAT-208 Copilot needs synthetic focus-gained before submit: Agent brand detection and per-vendor hacks.
- CAT-451 PaneInfo.agent from effective_agent_label: Agent identity may be guessed by brand/screen detection.
- CAT-538 experimental.reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime (+ cjk_ime_agents, cjk_ime_cursor_shape): Per-agent-brand special-casing for human IME input.
- CAT-540 Config reload toast: Toast side effect; the report return value is the machine channel.
- CAT-602 codex unknown-status special case: Per-brand special case in readiness logic.
- CAT-615 --kind from agent registry: Brand-coded agent list baked into the binary.
- CAT-625 Integration targets: Agent brand list hardcoded in the CLI.
- CAT-688 server.agent_manifests / reload / update: These manifests drive agent-state detection by screen heuristics and brand rules, so state is guessed rather than reported.
- CAT-689 Agent manifest status fields: Documents detection rules keyed per agent brand.
- CAT-881 ClientShellNotificationEffect Sound/Terminal/System: It relies on agent brand detection and plays sounds.
- CAT-900 canonical agent via parse_agent_label: It depends on agent brand detection.
- CAT-1211 direct_graphics_profile_values: Terminal brand detection heuristic.
- CAT-1271 experimental.reveal_hidden_cursor_for_cjk_ime / cjk_ime_agents / cjk_ime_cursor_shape: Depends on agent brand detection by name and is an input-method workaround for humans.
- CAT-1289 ui.sidebar.agents.rows_by_agent: Layout selection keyed on detected agent brand.
- CAT-1291 AgentsSidebarConfig::rows_for_agent: Depends on agent detection (brand detection) to pick layout.
- CAT-1295 ui.sound.agents.<agent> (22 keys): Per-agent-brand keys; omp and mastracode have no key and always use Default.
- CAT-1296 SoundConfig::allows: Sounds gated on detected agent identity; screen-heuristic state drives them.
- CAT-1298 Default: droid sound Off: Hardcoded brand special case.
- CAT-1307 Screen-tail pattern matching as state source: Agent state is GUESSED from screen text, not reported by the agent; fragile to UI changes.
- CAT-1312 Agent enum (24 known agents): Brand detection: agent identity inferred from process, not declared by the agent; unknown agents are invisible.
- CAT-1316 identify_agent from process name: Brand detection by process name.
- CAT-1320 Hermes installer / Cursor bundled-node / Muse versioned-binary signatures: Brittle brand-specific argv fingerprints.
- CAT-1322 session_identity_only_integration: State for these agents still guessed from screen text.
- CAT-1342 Region specs: Regions encode TUI chrome layout (prompt boxes, rules, Codex prompt markers) of specific agents.
- CAT-1346 Prompt-marker regions are Codex-specific: Region logic tied to one brand's TUI glyphs.
- CAT-1368 host_modify_other_keys_mode env sniffing: Host brand detection via environment variables decides terminal protocol behavior.
- CAT-1373 non-Latin Ctrl chord rewritten to physical key: Matches one terminal (Ghostty) behavior by brand, a heuristic about the host.
- CAT-1374 WezTerm control associated text quirk: Per-terminal quirk workaround (brand-specific).
- CAT-1387 session-only hooks; lifecycle hooks removed: Herdr retreated from agent-reported lifecycle to session-id capture only, which implies state is inferred (likely screen detection) for these agents.
- CAT-1403 print_outdated_update_notice: A stderr nag aimed at a human; no structured form of the same data in this file.
- CAT-1411 Claude legacy hook removals: Herdr no longer receives Claude working/blocked/idle from hooks; state must come from another mechanism (unknown here).
- CAT-1514 AppEvent::AgentProcessDetected: Agent brand detection by process inspection; it identifies an agent by guessing.
- CAT-1515 AppEvent::CodexPromptObserved: A screen-text heuristic for one agent brand.
- CAT-1551 codex_prompt_ready: Agent brand detection by prompt text; breaks on copy changes
- CAT-1569 agent_osc_title: Feeds brand/state guessing from terminal title text.
- CAT-1626 Process-specific Droid ED3 filter test: Brand-specific agent detection by process cmdline existed; shows agent-name heuristics in the pane path.
- CAT-1664 managed_agent_kind: Agent brand-keyed detection (crate::detect::agent_label) baked into persisted data.
- CAT-1684 Restored agent seeded Idle: Initial state is assumed, not reported by the agent; guess based on agent brand label.
- CAT-1698 foreground_job: Feeds agent-state detection by guessing from process names/argv instead of an explicit status protocol.

- CAT-2406 show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders: Agent brand labels on chrome; manual label is the stable one.

- CAT-2509 AppEvent::AgentProcessDetected / CodexPromptObserved: Agent brand detection from process and screen text.
- CAT-2562 [update] channel, version_check, manifest_check: A background network phone-home, and a remotely updated agent-detection manifest, imply screen-heuristic detection of agents.
- CAT-2567 [ui.toast] delivery and [ui.sound]: Toasts and sounds are human-attention channels.
- CAT-2568 [experimental] CJK IME cursor reveal and cjk_ime_agents: Agent brand detection is hardcoded by name.

- CAT-2595 detect_backend: Env-var terminal brand sniffing; headless or unknown hosts silently get nothing.
- CAT-3011 Screen-based brand detection: Agent brand detection and screen-text heuristics are explicitly agent-unfriendly by rubric.
- CAT-3021 Background-agent signals: Delegation activity is visible but inferred from screen text.
- CAT-3025 OSC title and progress signals: Signals are used by the manifest but agent brand/state support is agent-detection by rubric.
- CAT-3529 detach_key in config.toml (e.g. ctrl+]): Keyboard-only human feature.

## Client-pain list

All 846 client-pain catalog rows: behavior a programmatic client must work around.


### herdr / api

- CAT-007 server.ssh_agent.register: Registers a remote-host agent socket; lasts only until this API connection closes
- CAT-013 NotificationShowReason: Why a toast was or was not shown, including RateLimited and NoForegroundClient
- CAT-025 Strict enum parsing: Test asserts future_status is rejected for AgentStatus
- CAT-040 pane.move focus default true: PaneMoveParams.focus defaults true unlike split which defaults false
- CAT-042 pane.process_info: Takes optional pane_id (not target); returns shell_pid, foreground_process_group_id, tty, foreground_processes with argv/cmdline/cwd
- CAT-044 pane.read: Snapshot read with source, lines, format, strip_ansi; PaneReadResult has revision and truncated
- CAT-049 events.subscribe: Opens long-lived stream with typed subscriptions; returns SubscriptionStarted then event envelopes
- CAT-056 EventHistoryError Lost/Unavailable: events_after_checked returns Lost if requested sequence is older than the retained window; Unavailable on poisoned lock
- CAT-057 EventHub::push: Silently drops event when mutex poisoned; events_after returns empty on poison
- CAT-060 One request per connection in ApiClient: request_value connects, writes one line, reads one line and drops the stream
- CAT-064 status probe deadline reader: Status probe polls 2ms with deadline since Windows named pipes lack read timeouts; send/recv timeouts best-effort on Windows
- CAT-070 Unknown method rejected: Deserializing unknown method fails with unknown variant
- CAT-072 CONNECTION_POLL_INTERVAL 100ms: All waits/subscriptions poll at 100 ms cadence rather than being pushed; bounds event latency.
- CAT-073 APP_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT 5s: Max time the server waits for the app thread to answer an internal dispatch (probes, reads, gets).
- CAT-074 INITIAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT 5s: Client must send a full request line within 5 s of connecting or connection errors with TimedOut.
- CAT-075 MAX_INITIAL_REQUEST_BYTES 1 MiB: A request line over 1 MiB is rejected with InvalidData and the connection drops without a JSON error reply.
- CAT-078 ssh_agent_registration capability unix-only: Capability is true only on unix when the SshAgentRegistry could be built; else false and inherited pane env is retained.
- CAT-079 Newline-delimited JSON request: one request line per connection: handle_connection_with_stop reads one JSON line {id,method,params}, answers, and for ordinary methods closes the connection.
- CAT-081 server.ssh_agent.register (unix): Registers an SSH agent socket path; replies Ok then holds the connection open, refreshing the lease every poll until the client disconnects; lease ends with the connection.
- CAT-083 events.subscribe is all-or-nothing, set once: Subscriptions list is fixed in the single request; any setup error (e.g. invalid_regex, pane_not_found) rejects the whole stream, and no further requests are read on that connection.
- CAT-092 client_shell.surface.set is connection-local only: Over the normal API socket it returns connection_local_only; it only works through a client shell endpoint.
- CAT-097 Socket path resolution (tests): Socket path: explicit env override > named-session dir; default is the config dir even when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set.
- CAT-101 Output-matched is edge-triggered and sampled: Re-reads the pane each poll (not event history); fires once on transition to matching and re-arms only after a non-matching poll.
- CAT-103 match_output is line-based: Substring/regex tested per line; returns first matching line only; multi-line patterns cannot match.
- CAT-109 events_lost error: If a subscriber falls behind the retained event history the stream ends with error events_lost: "resubscribe and resync with session.snapshot".
- CAT-121 Windows prompt dispatch uses caller timeout: On Windows agent.prompt dispatch is bounded by the remaining wait timeout; elsewhere it is unbounded.
- CAT-122 events.wait only supports pane agent status: Other EventMatch kinds return unsupported_event_wait_match; pane_not_found aborts; other probe errors are ignored until timeout.

### herdr / app

- CAT-132 focus_pane_in_workspace switches visible UI: Focusing a pane switches the active workspace and tab, sets layout focus, and marks the session dirty; returns false if already focused or pane unknown.
- CAT-139 Zoom focuses the target pane: apply_pane_zoom first focuses the pane (focus_changed reported) and refuses zoom for single-pane tabs.
- CAT-140 Implicit group close confirmation: confirm_implicit_worktree_group_close requires confirm_close config and a group close; the confirmation is a TUI prompt.
- CAT-154 Host-local events bypass AppState: TerminalBell and ClipboardWrite are intercepted by HeadlessServer and forwarded to the foreground client; reducer returns empty.
- CAT-161 toast_config.delivery: Only ToastDelivery::Herdr sets the in-TUI toast; other modes leave delivery to the client notification.
- CAT-163 handle_pane_died: PaneDied cancels pending notification, drops plugin records, removes aliases, removes the pane, closes the workspace if last pane, preserves active/selected by id, falls back to Navigate mode when no workspaces remain.
- CAT-165 Resume waits for host theme: Resume does not start while host_terminal_theme is empty unless allow_empty_theme; deadline PENDING_AGENT_RESUME_THEME_WAIT.
- CAT-166 Stable inner rect width-1: For panes wider than 4 columns, the PTY width is shrunk by 1 column to match visible rendering.
- CAT-175 Single global view override, not per client: agent_view_override lives in AppState: one view for the whole server, so a second setter silently replaces the first.
- CAT-187 Focusing marks agent state as seen: focus_agent_target calls mark_active_tab_seen, turning done into idle.
- CAT-192 Agent start launches by typing into a shell: start_agent builds a shell command line with interactive_shell_command and submits it as input into the pane shell rather than spawning a process directly.
- CAT-193 agent.start requires an available shell pane: Pane that already hosts an agent/managed agent, or has no detectable shell, yields agent_pane_busy; pane id must be the current public pane id.
- CAT-198 Ambiguous target errors include candidate list: agent_target_ambiguous / agent_name_taken messages embed terminal_id, pane_id, workspace_id, tab_id, cwd, status for each candidate, as text inside `message`.
- CAT-207 Codex Windows paste-burst workaround: On Windows, a Right key is appended after Codex prompts to flush the paste burst before Enter.
- CAT-210 agent.read returns revision 0 and is a snapshot: PaneReadResult.revision hard-coded to 0; reads are point-in-time snapshots, not the attach stream.
- CAT-216 agent.wait: In app dispatch always returns invalid_request: handled by the api server, not by App.
- CAT-217 agent.prompt in sync dispatch: Returns invalid_request ("handled asynchronously by the app runtime"); only the deferred path serves it.
- CAT-218 worktree.list/open/create/remove sync dispatch: Return invalid_request because worktree work is asynchronous in the app runtime.
- CAT-219 server.ssh_agent_register: App path rejects with connection_local_only: requires a persistent local JSON API connection.
- CAT-220 server.live_handoff: Returns unsupported_in_app_mode: only the headless server supports live handoff.
- CAT-227 client.window_title.set/clear: App path returns changed:false with reason no_foreground_client.
- CAT-243 Agent exit handling: respawn shell or close pane: runtime_exit_action; non-Windows closes pane; Windows PowerShell respawns shell within 2s grace.
- CAT-251 replace closes old tab after build: Replacing a tab creates the new tab first, then closes the old one, removes plugin pane records and shuts down detached runtimes; old pane ids die (processes in them are terminated).
- CAT-254 layout export env is empty: Exported LayoutPane always has empty env and its command is the terminal launch_argv, so env and shell-started processes are not round-tripped; label is the manual label only.
- CAT-267 copy search limits: MAX_QUERY_BYTES=4096 and MAX_RETURNED_MATCHES=1024 (total stays exact).
- CAT-271 process_info tty: None: PaneProcessInfo.tty is hard-coded None in this handler.
- CAT-276 swap not-found is not an error: Missing swap source/target returns success with changed=false and reason not_found; cross-tab swap is refused (cross_tab).
- CAT-278 move refused when zoomed: Moving from a zoomed tab, or into a zoomed target tab, returns changed=false reason zoomed_tab; same-tab move returns same_tab.
- CAT-279 public_pane_id_aliases on cross-workspace move: When a pane changes workspace its old public id is aliased to the internal pane so previous_pane_id still resolves; public id may change otherwise.
- CAT-280 empty source workspace closed on move: Moving the last pane out of a workspace to another workspace removes the source workspace and reports closed_workspace_id.
- CAT-287 pane.read revision hard-coded 0: PaneReadResult.revision is always 0 and read ignores strip_ansi/intent shown in params; truncated reports omitted older rows.
- CAT-292 metadata stale seq silently ignored: Stale-sequence or post-process-exit metadata reports return success Ok without applying.
- CAT-299 confirmation_required on worktree group close: Closing a pane that would close a linked worktree group returns confirmation_required; restored group close may also be refused.
- CAT-301 pane_layout_snapshot: Snapshot rects include pane chrome (borders, gaps, outer borders) in terminal-cell units of the host terminal area; split ids look like split_<idx>_<path bits> or split_<idx>_root.
- CAT-313 Revision-validated pane coordinates (read_checked_pane_link): Rejects with `stale_target` if the pane is not visible on the active surface, and with `stale_content` if offset_from_bottom or content_revision differs, if content_seq is odd (mid-write), or if either changed during the read.

- CAT-317 Plugin logs are in-memory, capped at 200 per query: Logs come from `state.plugin_command_logs`, not disk; the query clamp is 200.

- CAT-349 Overlay and popup placement: Overlay spawns an overlay pane on the active pane; popup spawns a popup with optional width/height and labels the terminal with the manifest title. Popup returns plain Ok without pane info.

- CAT-508 Legacy bare tab id: `<ws>:4` (no `t`) is parsed as tab *position*, while `<ws>:t4` is public number; the two can refer to different tabs after a tab close.
- CAT-511 Legacy pane syntax treated as name for agents: `resolve_agent_target("p_1")` treats legacy `p_N` pane syntax as an agent *name*, not a pane id.
- CAT-514 pane.close confirmation: `PaneClose` returns error code `confirmation_required` when closing a pane would close a parent worktree group; selection and workspaces untouched.
- CAT-515 notification.show: `NotificationShow {title, body?, position?, sound}` returns `{shown, reason}` with reason Shown / Disabled (toast delivery Off) / Busy (an existing toast is not replaced) / RateLimited (`last_api_notification_at`).
- CAT-526 Popup agent detection disabled and no pane identity: Popup panes spawn with `AgentDetection::Disabled` and `PaneLaunchEnv::without_pane_identity()` so HERDR pane env vars are not set in the popup.
- CAT-528 direct_attach_resize_locks: Set of terminal ids whose size is owned by a direct attach client; server will not resize those.
- CAT-539 request_client_config_reload: Flag set after any config reload so attached clients reload their client-local sound/keybinding config from disk.
- CAT-546 server_hangup_probe: Function pointer (`platform::server_hangup_is_recent`) uses process-global SIGHUP evidence to decide whether exit was a hangup; tests stub it false.
- CAT-549 ViewState: Geometry (`terminal_area`, `pane_infos`) of the server-rendered active-tab pane surface; empty until a client renders.
- CAT-556 Resolver handle semantics differ per method: `resolve_terminal_target` matches the effective agent label and terminal_id. `resolve_agent_target` matches neither, and a pane id there must be an agent terminal. A client must pick the identifier form per RPC.
- CAT-563 Theme sync depends on the attached host terminal: Host theme and appearance come from the foreground client's terminal. A headless or programmatic client may send neither, and then panes get no `?997` reports (the None case).
- CAT-567 Status commands unsupported on some platforms: `status_commands_supported()` gates command entries. Where it is false they are silently dropped.
- CAT-569 Worktree remove shutdown policy: Terminal runtimes in the workspace are shut down before worktree removal when `force` is set, or always on Windows. Otherwise runtimes stay alive.
- CAT-571 Focus switch after worktree removal: Closing the active linked-worktree workspace changes the active workspace on the server. A client that tracks focus must re-sync.

### herdr / cli

- CAT-576 herdr terminal attach <terminal_id> [--takeover]: Direct attach to a terminal by id; --takeover forces the pane from its current holder.
- CAT-582 One request per connection via ApiClient: Each CLI call creates an api_client and request_value; socket closes after the answer so one connection per call.
- CAT-583 Server protocol version guard: Before each request the CLI pings the server for its protocol version and aborts with a mismatch JSON error and restart guidance if incompatible; send_request_unchecked skips it.
- CAT-587 Bare `help` operand quirk: `explain` and `wait` treat a literal `help` operand after the target as `--help`, so a target or text literally named help cannot be used there.
- CAT-601 agent.start readiness poll in CLI: CLI polls agent.get every 100ms; checks terminal_id pinned, kind matches, name still owns terminal; blocked => agent_not_ready; idle/done only ready when interactive_ready; codex unknown+interactive_ready accepted.
- CAT-603 agent_pane_busy retry: On agent_pane_busy the CLI retries up to 2s while the shell is still initializing and the terminal_id is unchanged.
- CAT-605 pane.process_info used for shell readiness: Calls pane.process_info with pane_id to see shell_pid equal to foreground process group and a shell name.
- CAT-606 No shell-init detection off unix: On non-unix the foreground process group is unavailable so busy start is never retried.
- CAT-611 --takeover disconnects other holder: `--takeover` forces attach, disconnecting whoever already holds the terminal.
- CAT-631 machine add: Parses target, --label, --remote-session (each once, `=` forms accepted); prepares remote install and starts its server before saving; failures leave nothing saved.
- CAT-634 Notification title help quirk: A title literally `help` is rewritten to the help subcommand.
- CAT-636 Three output modes: Leaf Output is Json (print response), Read (print_read_response), Quiet (send_ok_request, prints only errors).
- CAT-637 Fixed request ids: Each leaf uses a constant id such as cli:pane:list or cli:request, not a unique correlation id.
- CAT-643 pane.process_info: `pane process-info [--pane ID]` sends `pane.process_info` with pane_id.
- CAT-665 newer-client branch: Client newer than server: message says restart the server and appends caller-supplied restart guidance.
- CAT-682 `herdr terminal attach` / `session control` / `session observe`: `attach TERMINAL_ID [--takeover]`; `session control TARGET [--takeover] [--cols N] [--rows N]`; `session observe TARGET [--cols] [--rows]`. Observe is the non-owning mode.
- CAT-686 `server stop`: Remote machine: sends `server.stop` over the API. Local: calls `session::stop_active_server`.
- CAT-697 Remote status limits: For a `--machine` target, `server_binary_stale` becomes None and socket is reported as `machine:<id>/<session>`. A remote probe failure is an error rather than not_running.
- CAT-699 `--machine` allow-list: Allowed: workspace, worktree, tab, pane, notification; `agent` except `attach` and `explain --file`; `api snapshot`; `status server`; plugin link/unlink/enable/disable/list/action/log/pane; server stop/reload-config/agent-manifests/reload-agent-manifests. Everything else is rejected.
- CAT-700 `--machine` exclusivity: Cannot be combined with `--session`, `--remote`, or `--remote-keybindings`, nor specified twice. It uses the saved machine's session.
- CAT-703 Remote path rules: `remote_path_is_absolute` accepts `/`, UNC `\\`, and drive-letter paths. Plugin paths on a remote machine must be absolute.
- CAT-704 restart_guidance: Supplies the "restart the server" text; for a remote machine it warns that stopping the server exits its pane processes.
- CAT-714 Remote plugin paths: `normalize_plugin_path_arg` makes local paths absolute (tilde-expanded, cwd-joined). For a remote machine they must already be absolute.
- CAT-716 Plugin request id: Every plugin RPC uses the shared id `cli:plugin`, unlike the per-verb ids elsewhere.
- CAT-726 rename label rest-args: `label` collects rest args from position 1 verbatim, so `--flag` after id is part of the label
- CAT-733 Request ids `cli:workspace:<verb>`: Fixed string ids per command, not unique per call; report-metadata uses generic `cli:request`
- CAT-734 Last-wins / ordered map flags: Repeated `--cwd`, `--focus`/`--no-focus` resolve last-wins; `--cwd --literal` takes next token verbatim
- CAT-736 Help goes to stderr: Command list printed with eprintln, not stdout
- CAT-738 Quiet path uses send_ok_request: Sends only the Method and discards the body; one socket round trip per command
- CAT-746 Remote path rule: For a remote target, only absolute (POSIX, drive-letter, UNC) or `~`/`~/...` paths are accepted; relative paths error "remote worktree paths must be absolute or start with ~/"

### herdr / client

- CAT-754 AttachEscapeState is a unit stub on Windows: On Windows the escape state has no pending prefix and all attach input types are cfg(unix) only.
- CAT-755 Removing/disabling the active remote falls back to local with frozen presentation: If the active endpoint is retired, selection moves to Local, input is frozen and the shell shows the unavailable-local surface until a fresh surface arrives.
- CAT-757 write_remote_image_to_server: Sends ClientMessage::ClipboardImage{target, extension, data} to the server; images over MAX_CLIPBOARD_IMAGE_PAYLOAD are dropped with only a warn! and Ok(()).
- CAT-767 Endpoint command lane: one in-flight request per endpoint: Each endpoint has a queue plus a single in_flight command; others wait, and lanes are independent per endpoint.
- CAT-772 receive_chunk (chunked responses, final_chunk flag): Responses arrive in chunks (tests use 128 KiB) and are reassembled before JSON parsing; a 1.2 MB selection is not truncated.
- CAT-773 retire_lane cancels queued commands at source-off: At handoff the in-flight request is tombstoned and every queued request id is returned as cancelled; other endpoints are untouched.
- CAT-778 ActivationRollback (Pending, Unavailable(msg)): Rollback either pending a correlated request or unavailable, keeping pane input frozen while chrome and the error show.
- CAT-779 ACTIVATION_TIMEOUT 5 s: A handoff that does not complete in 5 s expires and rolls back.
- CAT-781 Endpoint must support surface interest: Old servers without supports_surface_interest are rejected with "endpoint must be updated before it can join the selected surface".
- CAT-783 start freezes input, source-off first, local never waits on remote: start freezes pane input; remote-to-remote sends focus-revoke then surface off and waits for ack; Local targets activate without remote ack.
- CAT-784 rollback closes the target transport when target-off is unacknowledged: If target release is not acknowledged it calls endpoints.fail(target) since closing is the only safe local revocation.
- CAT-790 endpoint_lease needs metadata for this connection generation: Fails with "endpoint metadata is not ready for this connection" until a snapshot identity arrives.
- CAT-795 TerminalHello (direct client): Direct terminal clients send `ClientMessage::TerminalHello{version,cols,rows,cell px,pixel_mouse}` and expect `Welcome{version,encoding,error}`. This is the same-install private protocol.
- CAT-806 Surface-interest requirement: An endpoint must support SURFACE_INTEREST and PRESENTATION_EFFECTS_FENCE capabilities plus the method `client_shell.surface.set`. Otherwise it is rejected as "needs a server update".
- CAT-811 Queue-full revokes the connection: On a full output queue the connection is aborted (ConnectionAborted) rather than dropping one message, because partial writes would break input ordering. Recovery goes through reconnect.
- CAT-812 Windows 512-byte write chunks: On Windows, nonblocking pipe writes are chunked to 512 bytes and the deadline resets on progress.
- CAT-817 connect_once rules: Local socket-not-found becomes a transient ConnectionRefused ("start its server"). SSH goes through `connect_saved_ssh`. The handshake must negotiate SemanticFrame. Non-local endpoints must support health check.
- CAT-823 Windows input path: Windows uses crossterm raw events converted to `ClientInputEvent` (Key, Mouse, Paste, FocusGained/Lost, HostDefaultColor). Several unix-only reader parameters are ignored there.
- CAT-828 No file transport off Unix: `FileTransport` has no ledger on non-Unix, so graphics always go inline.
- CAT-837 host_color_query_sent handshake: If the host theme query was sent, the pump arms a 1s window in which scan-code-zero Escape is treated as a host reply (OSC 10/11 default colors) rather than a keypress, then queries the host terminal theme
- CAT-839 WindowsInputHandoff backpressure: Keeps draining the console while the client queue is full; queued event groups are held, using try_reserve; returns false when the channel is closed. Comment: blocking would let OpenSSH/ConPTY lose pieces of raw VT reports
- CAT-840 mouse motion coalescing: Under backpressure consecutive single-event Moved, or same-button Drag, events with equal modifiers replace the previous pending one; clicks/keys are never dropped
- CAT-841 10ms poll and 64-record batch: WaitForSingleObject(handle,10) then ReadConsoleInputW up to 64 records per read; timeout produces Idle which flushes pending escape/raw state
- CAT-843 EscapeOrigin: HostReply (scan-code-zero Escape, belongs to a terminal reply) versus Keyboard (physical Escape or Ctrl+[)
- CAT-844 physical Escape deferral: A physical Escape press (scan code nonzero, no mods, repeat 1) is held in pending_physical_escape so a following "[<" (or "<") continues an SGR mouse report; otherwise Escape is emitted, then bytes processed
- CAT-845 default mouse (X10/legacy) candidate staging: While a legacy default mouse sequence (ESC [ M + 3 bytes) is pending, nested key records are staged; if it resolves to a mouse event the keys are consumed (including later releases), otherwise staged events are restored in order
- CAT-847 Windows Terminal paste Enter pair: Exact sequence ESC[13;28;13;1;0;1_ESC[13;28;13;0;0;1_ is replaced with CR inside pastes; other report-shaped payloads stay opaque
- CAT-853 idle flush ordering: On idle the win32 framer buffer, pending physical Escape, keyboard Escape (flush_keyboard_escape) and raw timeout bytes are flushed in that order; semantic events flush pending raw bytes first to preserve order
- CAT-854 Windows-only compile: All reader-loop, handle, trace and OS record code is cfg(windows); on other platforms only portable mapper/pump logic compiles (tests-gated translator)
- CAT-860 federated multi-machine viewing: When any SSH endpoint is enabled the client runs federated and keeps working if Local is down.
- CAT-861 Local server too old for federation: A federated client refuses a Local server that lacks the surface-interest capability and asks for a server update.
- CAT-862 ClientMessage::AttachTerminal{terminal_id, takeover}: Sent after the handshake when attaching directly to a terminal. `takeover` forces the attach.
- CAT-868 EndpointSupervisorEvent::Status / Connected: Supervisors report Online/Attention status with a generation counter. Connected hands over a reader/writer pair and the negotiation, then a reader thread starts.
- CAT-869 generation-gated message acceptance: A ServerMessage is dropped unless `write_stream.accepts(endpoint, generation)`. Retirement messages bypass the presentation gate.
- CAT-870 ServerMessage::ClientShellSnapshot unnegotiated: An unnegotiated binary snapshot is a protocol error for Local (fatal) or an attention state for federated/remote endpoints.
- CAT-876 ServerMessage::ClientShellEndpointResponseChunk: Chunked RPC responses for endpoint API requests issued from the shell, reassembled client-side.
- CAT-878 health ticking and Local-failure fatality: A timer tick runs `tick_health`. A failed Local transport is fatal when not federated. Otherwise it triggers disconnect and reconnect with a notice.
- CAT-883 dispatch_client_shell_actions gating: Endpoint requests are enqueued only for the active endpoint with an available surface, with the sole exception of `WorkspaceFocus` during activation. Otherwise the pending request is cancelled.
- CAT-884 endpoint activation as a transaction: Switching machines runs prepare, start, freeze presentation, wait for the coherent surface, then a presentation-sync epoch. Failures roll back, and input stays frozen until ownership is proven.
- CAT-885 deferred Local activation: If Local metadata is not ready, the selection is stored in `deferred_local_activation` and resumed later, with the notice "Local is reconnecting".
- CAT-886 handoff unavailable chrome: When no endpoint is proven safe, pane input stays blocked and only a client-owned "unavailable" frame is drawn.
- CAT-887 handle_endpoint_disconnect / handle_endpoint_attention: A disconnect cancels queued requests, marks the endpoint, and rolls back a pending activation. Attention (protocol or auth problem) disconnects with a diagnostic.
- CAT-891 method support check: If the server does not support a method, the client shows "Action unavailable. Update and restart" and sends nothing.
- CAT-893 endpoint_cancelled on interruption: An in-flight request interrupted by a disconnect or handoff fails with "This server action was interrupted. Check its state before retrying."
- CAT-903 AGENT_VIEW_PROJECTION capability: The agent view is used only when the endpoint supports projection. Otherwise rows fall back to local sort.
- CAT-904 stale endpoint ordering: Offline endpoints' cached rows are sorted last and excluded from `online_agent_targets`.
- CAT-914 Tab menu focuses tab before acting: activate_tab_context_action always pushes Method::TabFocus first, so right-click Close/Rename/New tab also steals focus to that tab.
- CAT-919 exit_copy_mode copy path: On copy, if no explicit selection is visible the current search match becomes an absolute_range selection; request_selection_copy runs (clipboard); selection is cleared and the pane scroll offset is restored via push_pane_scroll_offset.
- CAT-921 Per-client "Done" presentation projection: EndpointAgentPresentation rewrites agent_status: Idle/Done becomes Done until this client has acknowledged the agent state_change_seq by presenting a focused, coherent surface; otherwise Idle. Aggregated tab/workspace status is recomputed by status_priority.
- CAT-923 acknowledge_surface rules: A surface acknowledges agent completions only if the host terminal is not known unfocused (outer_focused != Some(false)), boot_id matches, and snapshot.revision == surface.projection_revision; acknowledgements are tracked per pane.
- CAT-927 focus_or_activate routes to RPC or endpoint switch: For the active endpoint it sends Method::WorkspaceFocus/TabFocus/PaneFocus; for another endpoint it emits ClientShellAction::ActivateEndpoint{endpoint_id, target}; offline non-local endpoints trigger a reconnect attempt and "is not ready".
- CAT-931 In-flight requests lost on disconnect: On disconnect all pending requests of the active endpoint are cancelled, integration installs reset, and scroll queues cleared.
- CAT-935 Snapshot commands filtered, agent recency computed: Unknown command actions are dropped; agent_recency assigns a client-side monotonically increasing rank when an agent state_change_seq changes across all endpoints.
- CAT-936 host_focus_baseline defaults to focused: When the terminal cannot report focus (outer_focused None), the client assumes focused and sends an explicit true baseline on activation.
- CAT-940 Kitty graphics: direct-asset trust and checkpoints: Graphics state is scoped (set_scope "local:unavailable"), direct assets are accepted only after trust_direct_graphics_asset(key, image_id); checkpoints can be restored; hidden when endpoint_error is set, Popup when a popup is shown. Unix only.
- CAT-941 Compose gating on matching snapshot and surface: compose returns None while pending_pane_surface exists, the pane surface generation differs from the active snapshot generation, or snapshot.revision != surface.projection_revision; with no snapshot/surface it renders an "<label>: <status>. Select a connected machine." frame.
- CAT-946 Link-activate fallback replay: While a PaneLinkActivate is pending, Drag/Up mouse events are appended to fallback_events and replayed to the pane if the server says no link was hit (url_click_consumes_until_up suppresses the rest of the gesture).
- CAT-950 Linked worktree workspaces cannot be reordered directly: Moving a workspace whose worktree.is_linked_worktree is true yields no method; only root workspaces (and their block) move.
- CAT-964 Retryable = saved remote machine awaiting backoff: machine_retryable is true only for non-local endpoints whose status is Connecting, Reconnecting or Attention.
- CAT-965 ClientMessage::ClientShellFocus {focused}: On outer terminal focus gain/loss the shell tells the server its focus; focus gain also queries host appearance, may repaint, and acknowledges agents in the active surface.
- CAT-969 Keys are queued while a copy operation is in flight: handle_key pushes keys into copy_input_queue when copy_operation_in_flight is true.
- CAT-975 Notification queue cap of 8, oldest dropped: At most 8 queued toasts; overflow pops the oldest; a new event for the same pane replaces earlier pending/queued/visible ones.
- CAT-989 path_for_local_endpoint: File state_dir/client-shell/local-<FNV-1a 64 hex of socket path>.json; each server socket gets its own preferences file.
- CAT-1023 pending_pane_surface exact-pair rule: A surface whose projection_revision is ahead of the snapshot waits in `pending_pane_surface`; the visible surface is always an exact (snapshot, surface) pair.
- CAT-1024 set_pane_surface revision gating: Drops surfaces with wrong boot_id, projection_revision below snapshot.revision, or older (projection, surface) revision than current; revision == snapshot+1 is parked as pending.
- CAT-1025 next-revision speculative surface: `projection_revision == snapshot.revision + 1` is stored as pending and hit targets are cleared until the matching snapshot arrives.
- CAT-1026 apply_active_snapshot: Ingests a ClientShellSnapshot; ignores a lower revision from the same boot_id and generation; resets pending surface when connection generation changes ("screen revisions restart per connection").
- CAT-1030 ActivateEndpoint: Switches the active machine (local or SSH profile) optionally focusing a target; multi-endpoint client.
- CAT-1035 reset_endpoint_projection: On endpoint switch clears hits, leases, pending requests, scroll queues, selection, copy mode, notices and errors.
- CAT-1058 confirmation_required server error: Server may reject close with code `confirmation_required` ("closing this tab would close a worktree group"); client converts it to a ConfirmClose overlay and on accept sends `workspace.close` with `close_group: true` (or false for a plain workspace).
- CAT-1061 server error becomes client overlay: An RPC error `confirmation_required` after `pane.close` renders a client-owned "Close workspace?" overlay and then `workspace.close` by stable id.
- CAT-1063 PaneSurfacePatch application: Incremental patch applies only if boot_id, projection_revision, base_surface_revision match and surface_revision == current+1; popup or graphics placements/retained assets force rejection; panes must exist with identical geometry; rows must lie inside a pane inner_rect or scrollbar rect.
- CAT-1064 ClientPaneSurfacePatchOutcome: Result is Rejected (caller must request a full surface) or Applied(Option<composed patch>).
- CAT-1070 Copy motions chained and queued: Keys pressed during a pending copy motion queue; y copies only after the motion result arrives (no actions emitted until then)
- CAT-1082 Disconnect cancels worktree dialog: mark_endpoint_disconnected drops pending requests and returns dialog to non-creating state before reconnect; only the disconnected endpoint is affected
- CAT-1083 Dispatcher cancels on frozen surface or failed send: Requests are cancelled when the target surface is frozen or transport send fails (BrokenPipe)
- CAT-1085 Presentation fence blocks sends: Navigation is queued while input is frozen (freeze_input/unfreeze_input) and delivered to the target after the fence; inactive surface raises 'Action interrupted' notice
- CAT-1088 Disconnected active endpoint freezes surface: Cached UI is shown stale (dimmed, '◐ reconnecting'), hits cleared, cursor hidden, pending integration installs reset
- CAT-1090 Surface waits for exact snapshot revision: A pane surface with projection_revision ahead of the snapshot is held pending until the snapshot with that revision arrives
- CAT-1091 Reconnect new-generation surface revisions: Surface/projection revision counters may restart low after reconnect with same boot_id; agent_scroll is preserved
- CAT-1097 Direct graphics unix only: Graphics and image tests are cfg(unix); some notification-click tests are cfg(windows)
- CAT-1099 Offline cached navigator targets disabled: Cached navigator and mobile targets of a non-online machine are marked stale, dimmed and not activatable
- CAT-1101 Workspace drag rejects foreign slots: Dragging a workspace onto a foreign endpoint slot is rejected
- CAT-1109 endpoint rejection notice with error code and 3s deadline: An `Err(ClientShellEndpointError{code,message})` becomes a `Rejected` notice keyed `method:code` (e.g. `workspace.focus:not_found`). It carries the server message and a ~3s deadline. A paste rejection is keyed `paste_rejected`.
- CAT-1110 endpoint_timeout becomes a deduplicated Timeout notice: Error code `endpoint_timeout` yields `ClientEndpointNoticeKind::Timeout` keyed by method. The body names the method.
- CAT-1117 prefix is kept local and prefix+q detaches: The prefix key (0x02) produces no request. `q` after it sets `detach=true` with no request sent.
- CAT-1118 key press/release pairing keeps press target: A release goes to the pane that received the press. This holds when Shift is released first, around IME commits and focus loss, and for non-Latin Ctrl chords. A release is never a repeat, and an unmatched release does not take another held key.
- CAT-1122 host profiles: Kitty host pushes `>7u` or `>31u`: `HostProfile::Kitty` pushes keyboard flags 7, or 31 when the pane asks for all keys reported. `Legacy` pushes nothing.
- CAT-1123 conformance baselines (ratchet): Known failures are capped at: keyboard 60, mouse 96, split-idle 207, Windows records 1. Remaining cases are Alt+] and similar behind legacy hosts. Their bytes start host replies and are never forwarded, and the reply-tail discard can swallow the next key (#344).
- CAT-1124 split reads of ESC[ are ambiguous with Alt+[ on legacy hosts: `split_read_robustness` tries every cut point of a corpus. Burst splits must decode like the whole input. Idle splits after a 50ms pause still mismatch on legacy hosts.
- CAT-1128 WezTerm escape tap preserves doubled ESC: A press of `\x1b` followed by a release of `ESC[27;1:3u` reaches the pane with the doubled escape kept.
- CAT-1129 mouse transparency across tracking and format modes: `MOUSE_TRACKING` and `MOUSE_FORMATS` tables and `GESTURES` are checked against a mouse oracle on a 40x10 pane. The host is set to `?1003h ?1006h`.
- CAT-1130 Windows ConPTY win32-input-mode records: On Windows, native key records are forwarded to the pane ConPTY when the pane has negotiated no keyboard protocol. The tests cover the `us` and `de` layouts.
- CAT-1133 mobile layout below ~44 cols: 2-row header, rest pane: `layout(44,20)` reserves a 2-row `mobile_header`. `surface_size` returns `ClientSurfaceSize{cols:44, rows:18}`, so the server sizes the pane for the remainder.
- CAT-1140 PaneSurfaceFrame: Surface frame carries boot_id, projection_revision, surface_revision, a cell frame with cursor state, per-pane rect/inner_rect/scrollbar_rect/scroll/mouse_reporting/sgr_pixel_mouse/alternate_screen_active/pixel size, splits, popup, graphics scene. This is the rendered truth the client composes.
- CAT-1142 ClientShellAction::ReplayMouse: When link lookup yields no url, the client replays the captured mouse events locally (PaneFocus then selection).
- CAT-1145 Stale word-lookup replies discarded: Row replies are ignored after typing, new click, focus/content change, resize, or reconnect content changes.
- CAT-1154 Held key repeats suppressed while popup pending: Pending popup suppresses held pane repeats but keeps release; on close repeats are re-processed into the focused pane.
- CAT-1155 Popup command pending state: Custom command with `CustomCommandAction::Popup` sets `popup_pending`, blocks underlying input until surface arrives, an error returns, or `popup_pending_deadline` times out.
- CAT-1156 Projection/surface revision gating: Shell refuses a surface whose projection_revision mismatches the snapshot and clears hits either order; compose returns None.
- CAT-1158 PaneSurfacePatch (retained surface patch): Incremental patch with base_surface_revision, surface_revision, rows, panes, cursor updates only pane cells without recomposing chrome; stale base returns `Rejected` and leaves the surface untouched.
- CAT-1161 Failed dismiss reopens authoritative snapshot: If dismiss errors (e.g. `stale_announcement`) the overlay reopens and the local dismissed marker is cleared; endpoint snapshot is authority.
- CAT-1165 Onboarding completion writes `onboarding = false`: Completing onboarding rewrites the local TOML (`local_config_path`) setting `onboarding = false`, preserving other keys like `[terminal] default_shell`; write failure sets config_diagnostic "failed to read config" but still proceeds.
- CAT-1171 Pending navigation highlight until authoritative focus: A local navigation request keeps its highlight until the server reports focus (revision-tagged); failure/cancel/identity change/new intent releases it.
- CAT-1174 run_terminal_attach(terminal_id, takeover): Direct attach of a PTY terminal by id; takeover flag forces the attach; uses AttachEscapeState so a human escape sequence detaches.
- CAT-1175 run_terminal_attach on Windows: Returns ErrorKind::Unsupported "direct terminal attach is not supported on Windows yet" (gated by platform::capabilities().direct_terminal_attach).
- CAT-1180 takeover on ControlTerminal: takeover:true asks the server to evict the existing controller.
- CAT-1182 invalid control input is ignored: A bad JSON line prints "terminal session control input ignored" to stderr and the loop continues; blank lines skipped.
- CAT-1183 connect_terminal_session_stream handshake: Handshake uses no pixel capabilities, no mouse; requires encoding RenderEncoding::TerminalAnsi, otherwise exit(1). Connect failure exits the process.
- CAT-1186 Graphics and other server messages dropped: ServerMessage::Graphics and all other variants are silently ignored in session output; clean EOF returns Ok.
- CAT-1191 terminal.mouse {action,button,column,row,modifiers}: Actions down/up/drag/move, buttons left/right/middle, cell position; server encodes for pane mouse mode and drops if app has no mouse reporting.
- CAT-1193 presentation_frozen handoff: During a source-off-first endpoint handoff the blitted frame stays authoritative until an acknowledged target snapshot/surface commits; frame presentation returns false while frozen.
- CAT-1197 Host capability probe (CSI ?1016$p, ?u, c): Writes DECRQM 1016, kitty keyboard query and DA1; waits up to 250 ms, buffers up to 64 KiB of stdin; DA1 reply terminates the probe.
- CAT-1207 word selection via pane.selection_read: Double-click-hold selects words by fetching one row at a time through PaneSelectionRead with content_revision, one request in flight, latest pointer wins.
- CAT-1212 ClientError Display + reattach hints: ConnectionFailed, HandshakeRejected{version,error}, ServerShutdown{reason}, ConnectionLost; detached shutdown suggests `herdr`, `herdr session attach <name>`, or REATTACH_COMMAND_ENV_VAR command.
- CAT-1217 optional surface_reuse Decoder: If negotiated, each decoded message passes through protocol::surface_reuse::Decoder, which rewrites compact/reused surface frames into full messages.
- CAT-1219 Decode failure is a disconnect: Surface-decoder errors are mapped to Io InvalidData framing errors, which fall to the generic error arm and tear the endpoint down.
- CAT-1220 Read error logged and disconnects: Any other framing/IO error emits warn "server read error" then ServerDisconnected; no retry inside the thread.
- CAT-1224 Registry send is fire-and-forget: Via the registry, a write failure is not reported to the caller; it surfaces later as a lifecycle transition.
- CAT-1228 Tests are cfg(all(test, unix)) only: The only coverage for transport runs on Unix; Windows named-pipe behavior is untested here.

### herdr / config

- CAT-1237 app_dir_name differs by build profile (herdr-dev vs herdr): cfg!(debug_assertions) switches the directory name so a debug binary never shares config/state with release.
- CAT-1239 Config::load startup loader (all-or-nothing fallback to defaults): On read or parse error the whole config falls back to Default with a "using defaults" diagnostic string; unknown keys only warn.
- CAT-1267 [advanced] scrollback_limit_bytes (default 10000000, alias scrollback_lines): Per-pane scrollback cap in bytes; the legacy lines alias parses into the same field.
- CAT-1269 [experimental] allow_nested: Allows launching herdr inside an existing herdr pane; default false.
- CAT-1276 keys.remote_image_paste (ctrl+v): Local-client shortcut sending a clipboard image to a remote herdr session.
- CAT-1278 KeysConfigOverlay with extra_prefixes for cross-version compatibility: Local keybind profile serialized for endpoint clients; older clients read prefix as one string and ignore extra_prefixes, newer clients merge it.
- CAT-1283 prefix keys reserved; prefix twice sends literal prefix: Any binding using the prefix key as RHS is rejected ("reserved keybinding").
- CAT-1285 layout-aware matching for shifted/Unicode keys and legacy uppercase events: terminal_key_matches_combo uses shifted_codepoint, legacy shifted ASCII letters and shifted number symbols so non-US layouts and kitty/legacy terminals match.
- CAT-1306 update_file_at (read-modify-write): Creates config dir, reads current config (empty if missing), applies edit, overwrites with std::fs::write; text-level upsert preserves other content; not atomic (no temp+rename) and no locking, so concurrent writers can race.

### herdr / detect

- CAT-1310 visible_blocker overrides non-blocked integration state: Live blocking chrome on screen is stronger than prompt-like scrollback and can override a non-blocked hook-reported state.
- CAT-1311 visible_working is diagnostic; PTY activity is working authority: Screen "working" chrome is only metadata / non-PTY fallback; PTY output activity is the normal authority for Working.
- CAT-1324 Default catalog URL: https://herdr.dev/agent-detection/index.toml is fetched for remote manifests.
- CAT-1330 Fetch via external curl process: Network fetch shells out to curl (noninteractive curl_command); no curl means update fails.
- CAT-1336 Known-agent no-match defaults to Idle: When a known agent matches no rule (or has no manifest), state=Idle with fallback_reason "default_known_agent_idle_fallback".
- CAT-1345 Process-global manifest cache with explicit reload: OnceLock<RwLock> cache of compiled rules; detection uses cached manifest until reload_manifests/reload_manifests_for_agents; reload serialized by mutex; poisoned locks recovered.
- CAT-1348 Test: end-anchored footer gates allow only auxiliary tail: Live controls count only near bottom; newer prompt/output makes controls historical.

### herdr / input

- CAT-1360 remove_sole_text_press: A release for a text press (`?` released as `/` after Shift) cannot be matched by identity; it is paired only when that forwarded text press is the sole lease held for the source. Otherwise nothing is taken.
- CAT-1362 HostGeometry: Host terminal size in cells and pixels; `new` returns None if any dimension is zero (hosts that do not report pixel size give no geometry).
- CAT-1363 HostGeometry::current is unix-only: Queries `crossterm::terminal::window_size()`; defined only under `cfg(unix)`, so no pixel geometry on Windows.
- CAT-1364 WindowsKeyRecord (serde): Serializable Windows console key record: `key_down`, `repeat_count`, `virtual_key_code`, `virtual_scan_code`, `unicode`, `control_key_state`. `Serialize/Deserialize` implies it can cross the client/server wire.
- CAT-1369 KeyboardProtocol Legacy/Kitty{flags}: Active host keyboard protocol; zero kitty flags means Legacy; `reports_event_types` checks flag bit 2, `reports_all_keys` bit 8. Without event types, releases and repeats do not exist and leases cannot pair.
- CAT-1372 mouse protocol enums unix-only: `MouseProtocolMode`/`Encoding` are gated `cfg(any(unix, test))`, so Windows builds have no child mouse-mode tracking.
- CAT-1375 legacy key parsing: `\r` Enter, `\t` Tab, `\x1b` Esc, `\x7f` Backspace, `\x1b\x7f` Alt+Backspace, `ESC x` Alt+x, uppercase ASCII gets Shift. A bare LF is intentionally not Enter (ambiguous; falls through to Ctrl+J). Multi-character data or unknown strings return None.

### herdr / integration

- CAT-1378 Windows install gate: `install_target_inner` refuses unsupported targets with "<label> integration is not supported on Windows".
- CAT-1380 frozen client IntegrationTarget enum: Letta is kept out of the API `IntegrationTarget` enum so old clients never receive an unknown variant; `EXPERIMENTAL_INTEGRATION_TARGET_LABELS = ["letta"]` lists CLI-only labels until the agent registry gives first-class registration.
- CAT-1381 OpenCode V2 deferred registration: `install_opencode` returns a message "to enable OpenCode V2, start opencode2 once, then reinstall" when `cli_config_path` is None, so install can need a second manual run.
- CAT-1394 home_dir failure: Errors with "home directory is not set; cannot locate home directory" when HOME (or Windows equivalents) is unset/empty.
- CAT-1408 hard-link rejection: Refuses to update a config with link count > 1: "config has multiple hard links; use a separate file or a symlink before retrying"; rechecked before commit.
- CAT-1409 not a multi-file transaction: `check_config_targets` is a preflight only; there is no cross-file transaction, so a failure midway can leave some files updated.
- CAT-1414 strict JSON and duplicate-key rejection: Claude settings are parsed with comments, trailing commas and single quotes disallowed; duplicate object keys at any depth are rejected ("contains duplicate key"). Install fails on invalid structure rather than rewriting.
- CAT-1418 Hermes YAML editor scope: Doc comment says it supports only the flat `plugins` and mapped `plugins.enabled` sequences; other YAML layouts are not handled and are left unchanged on disable.
- CAT-1419 cli.json registration deferred during migration: `add_cli_plugin` returns `None` when cli.json is absent and `tui.json` or `state/kv.json` exists, since OpenCode imports V1 prefs only while cli.json is absent.
- CAT-1420 OpenCode config shape validation: `validate_tui_plugin_config` fails if the root is not an object or `plugin`/`plugins` is not an array; install preflights this before touching assets.
- CAT-1446 install requires agent present: Most installers fail with "<agent> directory not found ... install <agent> first" when the config dir is missing. Mastracode is the exception: it creates its hooks dir and does no dir-exists check.
- CAT-1461 windows_supports_portable_integrations: Windows supports only a subset of targets, plus native availability checks.
- CAT-1472 opencode recovery copy blocks retry: A leftover `cli.json.herdr-backup` makes install and uninstall refuse ("recovery copy"), whatever the config state, and symlink referents are checked too.
- CAT-1479 install_*_errors_when_config_dir_missing (all targets): Every install errors when the agent's config dir does not exist. It never creates the agent's home. The exception is the Pi extensions dir, which is created if the agent dir exists.

### herdr / kitty_graphics

- CAT-1482 Source-file images skipped; headless graphics budget: Placements with source_file descriptors are not forwarded; headless transaction budget = MAX_GRAPHICS_FRAME_SIZE - MAX_FRAME_SIZE; image_transfer_estimated_size estimates base64 + overhead.
- CAT-1485 GraphicsOutput module doc: ordered, local-only output: Graphics bytes are emitted as an ordered operation list for the local host terminal only; upload pixels stay raw (not base64-chunked) until output I/O.
- CAT-1486 MAX_SURFACE_GRAPHICS_PLACEMENTS = 4096: Hard cap on placements in one scene sent to a client; collection stops at the cap.
- CAT-1491 ClientState holds scene, display_scene, assets, host cache: Client-side (TUI endpoint) mirror: authoritative scene from server, a display_scene that may lag to avoid blank frames, resident raw assets, host cache, trusted direct images, stale/forced-delete lists.
- CAT-1492 Image id namespaces: Terminal-sourced images use native ids (0x4000_0000 / 29-bit hash); direct/API images use 10_000 + hash mod 900_000. Hash-derived, scoped by `scope`, collisions possible.
- CAT-1493 ClientState::set_scope: Changing scope (per boot/connection of the host terminal) clears scene, assets, trusted direct, and forces a host-wide delete (reset_pending).
- CAT-1496 ClientState::encode_output: Produces ordered GraphicsOutput: cleanup, stale deletes, then placement pieces. If cell pixel size is unknown or scope is empty, emits only a host clear (no graphics).
- CAT-1497 native_host_image_id / host_image_id: Deterministic id derivation from scope+source (native) or scope+full key (direct), keeping namespaces disjoint.
- CAT-1498 collect_scene: Server-side builder: from the app, tab surface view, popup size, cell size and DeliveryCache, returns (SurfaceGraphicsScene, next DeliveryCache, SourceFiles). Returns empty scene when cell size unknown. `_client_id` is unused.
- CAT-1500 PaneLayer source frozen for old-server compat: SurfaceGraphicsSource::PaneLayer is no longer collected by current servers but kept in wire types; ClientSurface placements are skipped in collection.
- CAT-1502 HEADLESS_GRAPHICS_TRANSACTION_BUDGET per scene: Assets whose estimated encoded size exceeds the budget are skipped forever; others past the cumulative budget are deferred (pending=true) to later scenes.
- CAT-1505 Image formats Rgb/Rgba/Png map to kitty f=24/32/100: format_code and the descriptor mapping define the only supported pixel formats.
- CAT-1506 Unix-only direct-asset ack path: accepts/trust/retire_direct are cfg(unix); non-unix builds lack the direct file adoption path.

### herdr / pane

- CAT-1507 MIN_PANE_ROWS / MIN_PANE_COLS: Hard floor of 2 rows by 4 cols for any pane PTY size.
- CAT-1510 Outer agent identity env stripped: New panes remove CODEX_THREAD_ID, OMPCODE, CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN; launch env can re-add them on purpose.
- CAT-1531 PaneRuntime::foreground_cwd: cwd of the foreground group leader, falling back to a member whose cwd differs from the shell; returns None on non-unix.
- CAT-1532 PaneRuntime::resize: Clamps to MIN_PANE_ROWS/COLS, skips unchanged sizes, bumps content_seq under a write lock, resizes the terminal and PTY, and marks detection content changed.
- CAT-1537 PaneRuntime::try_send_bytes: Non-blocking enqueue of raw bytes to the PTY; a full queue gives TrySendError.
- CAT-1538 PaneRuntime::validate_input_submission: Preflights a complete API command against the PTY actor on unix; it is a no-op on Windows.
- CAT-1545 handoff_history_ansi: Primary-screen history as ANSI, truncated to MAX_REPLAY_BYTES_PER_PANE on a UTF-8 boundary; None on the alternate screen.
- CAT-1546 PaneRuntime::input_state: Terminal input mode state (kitty keyboard, bracketed paste, mouse), exposed only on unix.
- CAT-1558 Hyper/Meta chords not forwarded: Hyper and Meta modified keys return None; they are dropped instead of typed as the bare key
- CAT-1559 legacy_shell_key: For panes with no negotiated keyboard protocol, maps Ctrl+M/I/[ , modified Enter and Ctrl+Shift+letter to classic Enter/Tab/Esc/control bytes
- CAT-1560 legacy_super_chord: Super (Cmd) chords are not forwarded to panes that negotiated no keyboard protocol
- CAT-1564 Poisoned-lock fallback returns empty result: Most readers do lock().ok() and return default/empty (visible_text, input_state None); a poisoned reader lock gives a silent empty result.
- CAT-1575 Handoff seeding is unix-only: seed_handoff_input_state and keyboard seeding are cfg(unix); InputState itself is cfg(any(unix,test)).
- CAT-1585 modify_other_keys level 1 treated as none: libghostty tracks only level 2; level 1 behaves as if nothing negotiated, matching Ghostty.
- CAT-1590 Recent read range anchors on last content row or cursor: On primary screen the range ends at the greater of last non-blank row and cursor row; on alt screen it ends at physical end.
- CAT-1593 Windows recent-text fallback: On Windows, empty libghostty text falls back to a separate windows_recent_fallback cache; Unix has no such path.
- CAT-1596 synchronized_output_state: Returns (active, epoch); defaults to (true, 0) on lock failure.
- CAT-1601 suppress_native duplicate-reply suppression: With a 7-bit intro and raw-C1 ST the native ghostty parser keeps DCS open and later answers earlier keys again; herdr emits an empty `suppress_native` marker so only that dispatch's XTGETTCAP replies are dropped.
- CAT-1602 Native-DCS pending bookkeeping on ESC/CAN/SUB: While native_dcs_pending, ESC (0x1b), CAN (0x18) and SUB (0x1a) end the native dispatch and push a suppress marker, even inside ignored strings.
- CAT-1603 finalize(): multi-key query split: Splits body on `;` and emits one reply per known capability; unknown or malformed keys produce no reply (no `0+r` negative reply).
- CAT-1605 Capability list is static and partial: Only 8 caps are mirrored; no Co/colors, kitty keyboard etc. via this path.
- CAT-1606 CAN/SUB/ESC cancel preserves dispatch offsets: Test pins that a cancel byte inside an ignored string yields 3 replies with a suppress marker at the exact cancel offset.
- CAT-1608 Cache state struct: Holds rows, last_snapshot, `usable`, last_scrollbar, `needs_refresh`; usable=false means reads return an empty snapshot.
- CAT-1610 update(): primary-screen-only, bottom-only snapshotting: Skips entirely on alt screen; marks cache unusable when the viewport is scrolled up; blank snapshot clears and invalidates cache; identical snapshot with no history change is a no-op.
- CAT-1611 Deferred-refresh recovery via scroll probing: When a refresh is pending, temporarily scrolls the viewport page by page from the bottom (up to 2000 rows), merges pages, then scrolls back to bottom.
- CAT-1613 Alt screen yields empty recent text: primary_screen_active gate makes recent reads return nothing while an alternate-screen app runs.
- CAT-1615 unwrapped_text limits rows before unwrapping: Takes last `lines` rendered rows then unwraps, so a requested count of N may yield fewer than N logical lines and may cut a wrapped line's head.
- CAT-1616 visible_render_lines drops empty rows: Rebuilds visible rows via render-state iterator and skips rows whose text is empty, so blank lines are not preserved in the cache.
- CAT-1618 merge_snapshot overlap merge with cap: Appends new snapshot after longest suffix/prefix overlap with the cache and evicts oldest rows beyond 2000. Repeated identical rows can be ambiguously deduped.
- CAT-1619 Test: alt-screen snapshots ignored, old rows kept: After `ESC[?1049h` clear the cache still has earlier primary rows.
- CAT-1620 Test: output while scrolled up invalidates cache: If output arrives while the viewport is scrolled up, the fallback is marked unusable and both wrapped and unwrapped reads return empty.
- CAT-1627 ED2/ED3 semantics: ED2 clears display only; ED3 (`CSI 3 J` and `CSI ? 3 J`) clears history but keeps display; alt-screen ED3 does not touch primary history; synchronized output (`?2026`) redraw replays must not duplicate or leave old rows.
- CAT-1631 Sparse patches and viewport clipping: Patch lists only dirty rows (0-based y), clipped to requested height; rows outside clip stay dirty for the next collect.
- CAT-1632 Fallback on OSC 8 hyperlinks: A dirty patch containing hyperlink cells returns Fallback (full redraw) and previously collected rows stay dirty.

### herdr / persist

- CAT-1637 restore_handoff / handoff_pane_aliases (unix only): Server handoff restore keeps pane aliases across a server replacement; unix only.
- CAT-1640 load (session snapshot): Reads session.json; missing/read error/parse error/newer version all return None with structured tracing events (persist.restore outcome=missing/read_error/unsupported_version/parse_error).
- CAT-1642 Newer snapshot version ignored: File version > SNAPSHOT_VERSION is skipped, not migrated, with a warning that it is from a newer herdr.
- CAT-1648 plugin_registry::load lenient: Returns empty Vec on any failure so a corrupt registry never blocks server startup; mutations still use strict reads.
- CAT-1651 SessionWriter::save: Preserves unloaded file, takes periodic snapshot, saves session.json, then separately saves/clears history; failures only logged (session_save_failed) and history failure does not undo the committed layout.
- CAT-1667 migrate_workspace format sniffing: Errors if a workspace is neither current (identity_cwd) nor legacy (layout) shape, failing the whole parse.
- CAT-1671 restore: Rebuilds workspaces, terminals and runtimes from a snapshot; each pane gets a fresh shell in its saved cwd (processes are not preserved).
- CAT-1673 No handoff on non-unix: On non-unix, an imported runtime counts as a failed import; handoff APIs are cfg(unix).
- CAT-1675 Pane ids re-allocated on restore: restore_node_remapped assigns fresh globally unique PaneIds and returns old-to-new map; public numbers preserve addressing.
- CAT-1678 Unavailable pane preserved: If saved cwd is missing or shell fails to spawn, a placeholder terminal with restore_error is kept (label, argv, agent session, resume kept) instead of dropping the pane.
- CAT-1679 Missing saved directory blocks restore of pane: Pane with nonexistent cwd becomes an unavailable terminal with message to restore the directory and restart.
- CAT-1685 Managed agent identity only restored on handoff: agent_name/managed_agent are re-applied only for imported (handoff) runtimes or pending resume; plain fresh shells drop them.
- CAT-1686 Layout pruning after partial failure: Panes that could not be restored are pruned and splits collapse; tab with zero panes is dropped, as is a workspace with zero tabs.

### herdr / platform

- CAT-1688 socket_peer_pid (fallback): On unsupported platforms there is no way to learn which PID is on the other end of a local socket; returns None.
- CAT-1689 Unsupported-platform stubs for process introspection: foreground_job, foreground_group_leader_job, foreground_process_group_id, process_cwd, session_processes, signal_processes, process_start_token, live_pane_process_group, process_exists and available_pane_shell all return None/empty/no-op.
- CAT-1690 Unsupported-platform stubs for host integration: write_clipboard false, read_clipboard_text/image None, open_url Err(Unsupported), show_desktop_notification Ok(false), hostname/local_datetime None, status_commands_supported false.
