- CAT-1691 detach_server_daemon_command / current_process_is_detached_server_daemon (fallback): Server cannot be daemonised on unsupported platforms; detach is a no-op and detached check is always false.
- CAT-1707 validate_pty_submission: Before pane.send_input or agent start input, tcgetattr the PTY; in canonical mode it computes the longest line (after terminal translations) and rejects if over _PC_MAX_CANON, with message to wait for the shell prompt and retry; non-TTY is allowed.
- CAT-1711 Canonical preflight samples the mode at admission only: It bounds the current submission, not earlier incomplete input or later mode changes while input waits in the queue.
- CAT-1722 Launchd job needs GUI login session: Tests and the feature need gui/<uid> domain; absent domain means fallback to direct spawn where Cmd-Q can still kill the server.
- CAT-1728 Platform capability flags: capabilities(): live_handoff and direct_terminal_attach are true only on unix; preserve_legacy_doubled_escape_input only on macOS.
- CAT-1734 Remote bridge IDLE_TIMEOUT 60s: Bridge process exits with code 1 when no positive-byte I/O for 60s (suspend-inclusive clock); only unix linux/macos supported; legacy bridge has no deadline.
- CAT-1735 REMOTE_BRIDGE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SUPPORTED: Idle-timeout support is compile-time true only on linux and macos.
- CAT-1737 write_client_stream with progress timeout: If the stream has a write timeout, stalls past it shut the socket down and fail with TimedOut "terminal observer stopped receiving output".
- CAT-1740 No SSH multiplexing off Unix: shared_ssh_control_path returns Unsupported: interactive SSH recovery requires Unix OpenSSH multiplexing.
- CAT-1746 Probe before file medium: probe() writes a 4-byte file; prepare() returns None until the terminal consumes (deletes) it; a pending file unconsumed for 10s disables the ledger so the client uses inline images.
- CAT-1747 Image root fixed to /tmp: Does not use TMPDIR/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR because Ghostty only accepts /tmp (not /var/tmp).
- CAT-1754 Transient zero-sized grid error: terminal_grid_size returns ZeroSizedGridError when cols or rows is 0; resize watcher keeps last geometry rather than detaching, while startup rejects it.
- CAT-1763 allow_unelevated_clients (`--allow-unelevated-clients`): Sets a process-wide flag so an elevated server's pipe is labelled medium integrity instead of high.
- CAT-1764 local_server_security_descriptor: Builds the server descriptor: an integrity label `S:(ML;;NRNW;;;HI)` for an elevated server, or `ME` when unelevated clients are allowed or the server is unelevated. It blocks read and write from lower integrity levels.
- CAT-1765 local_server_connection_error: Rewrites PermissionDenied into a hint: use an administrator terminal, or stop and restart `herdr server` with `--allow-unelevated-clients`, which closes panes.
- CAT-1768 wait_client_stream_readable: Named-pipe reads have no timeout, so it sleeps at most 2 ms and callers peek before reading and check a cancellation flag.
- CAT-1771 write_config_temporary: Writes a new config temp file and syncs it. If the config already exists it fails with AlreadyExists ("config appeared while preparing a new file; retry the update").
- CAT-1772 prepare_paste_text_for_pty_platform: Normalizes pasted text to CRLF before writing to the PTY.
- CAT-1773 remote_ssh_config_paths: Returns `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\config` and `%PROGRAMDATA%\ssh\ssh_config` with `multiplexing: false`.
- CAT-1775 encode_windows_conpty_fallback: Encodes keys as Win32 input-mode CSI `ESC[vk;scan;unicode;down;ctrl;repeat_` for ConPTY, including special cases for bare Esc and Shift+Enter.
- CAT-1781 launch_server_daemon_command: If the current job kills processes on close, launches the server daemon through WMI `Win32_Process.Create` to escape the job; otherwise a plain spawn. Returns the pid.
- CAT-1786 live_pane_process_group: Returns the pid while the same process (matched by start token) is still running and belongs to the pane. Windows has no job control, so the pid stands in for the process group.
- CAT-1788 signal_processes: Any signal except Hangup is implemented as `TerminateProcess(pid, 1)`; Hangup is ignored.
- CAT-1789 write_clipboard: Writes UTF-8 text to the clipboard as Unicode text, owned by the console window. It rejects non-UTF-8 or NUL-containing bytes and returns false without a console window.
- CAT-1797 MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION / MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS: Rejects images wider or taller than 16384 px, or over 16M pixels total.
- CAT-1798 MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS (16 Mpx): Total pixel cap, enforced in validate_dimensions for both PNG and DIB inputs.
- CAT-1801 Supported DIB pixel formats: Only 24-bit BI_RGB, 32-bit BI_RGB, and 32-bit BI_BITFIELDS / BI_ALPHABITFIELDS are supported. Palette, 16-bit, 1/4/8-bit and RLE bitmaps return None.
- CAT-1802 LimitedWriter: An io::Write sink that fails with FileTooLarge ("encoded clipboard image exceeds protocol limit") once the output passes the cap.
- CAT-1805 check_recovery refuses on leftover backup: If a `.herdr-backup` or `.pending` file exists (checked with symlink_metadata), the update aborts with an actionable error naming the path.
- CAT-1806 Encrypted (EFS) config rejected: Configs with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ENCRYPTED are refused before any plaintext backup is made.
- CAT-1807 Multiple hard links rejected: The update is refused if nNumberOfLinks > 1, with the advice to use a separate file or a symlink.
- CAT-1809 No automatic rollback: A cleanup failure after the new contents are synced is reported but does not roll back.
- CAT-1811 show_actionable_desktop_notification(title, body, key, callback): Shows a toast keyed by `key` with a click callback. It lazily starts a service thread, with a 2s ready timeout and a 2s show timeout, and returns io::Result<bool>.
- CAT-1813 Per-executable URL protocol registration: Registers `herdr-notification-<sha256(exe path)[..8]>` under HKCU\Software\Classes. Its open command runs the bundled OpenConsole in headless mode, then `herdr --notification-activate "%1"`.
- CAT-1814 Requires bundled ConPTY runtime: register fails with NotFound unless conpty/x64/OpenConsole.exe sits next to the executable, so toasts do not work without it.
- CAT-1818 Power notifications fail open: If registration fails it logs at debug level and returns None, so the caller has no suspend or resume events.

### herdr / protocol

- CAT-1829 surface_active default true: Legacy hellos without the field are treated as having an active surface; unknown future fields ignored.
- CAT-1836 supports_required_codecs: Handshake accepts only clients listing all four v1 codecs; otherwise the server should reply incompatible.
- CAT-1839 endpoint.surface-reuse.v1: Surface message whose frame.cells is empty; client reuses cells from its retained baseline. Body is JSON {base_surface_revision, surface}.
- CAT-1840 CellBaseline / matches_patch: Per-connection baseline keyed by boot_id, projection_revision, surface_revision; a patch applies only if base_surface_revision equals the baseline and new revision is +1.
- CAT-1841 surface_reuse::Decoder::new / decode: Stateful decoder dispatching delta, scroll, reuse messages and updating baseline on PaneSurface and PaneSurfacePatch.
- CAT-1842 Reuse/delta/scroll without baseline is an error: Errors "without a baseline" / "does not match its baseline"; the Decoder returns Err and a client must request a full surface.
- CAT-1843 Patch mismatch silently clears baseline: A PaneSurfacePatch that does not match the baseline sets baseline = None rather than erroring; later reuse/delta messages then fail.
- CAT-1845 endpoint.surface-delta.v1: Binary (bincode) sparse delivery of a recomputed pane surface, base64 NO_PAD inside EndpointControl; layout frozen with the kind.
- CAT-1847 Decoder limits (grid dim 4096, 1,000,000 cells, 4096 panes/splits/split-path/assets, 65,536 hyperlinks/placements/retained assets): Hard caps on surface metadata; senders must mirror via metadata_fits or fall back.
- CAT-1848 Delta dimensions must match baseline: decode_for passes expected (width,height); mismatch rejected so a delta can never resize the grid.
- CAT-1849 endpoint.surface-scroll.v1: Scroll-aware patch: base64 of count byte, per-scroll x,y,w,h (u16 LE) + shift (i16 LE), then one framed PaneSurfacePatch; frozen layout.
- CAT-1850 Scroll only for committed pane geometry: Never scrolls a pane whose inner_rect or pane_id differs from the committed surface; both peers share geometry.
- CAT-1856 PROTOCOL_VERSION=22: Private same-install protocol version; exact match required, bumped on incompatible wire change.
- CAT-1857 Framing [u32LE len][bincode]: Every message is a 4-byte little-endian length then bincode (standard config) payload.
- CAT-1858 check_client_version: Rejects version 0, older, and newer; only exact PROTOCOL_VERSION match is Compatible.
- CAT-1859 ClientMessage enum: All client-to-server messages; variant order frozen for endpoint generation 1 (tag 0 TerminalHello, 1 Input, 2 ClipboardImage, 11 ClientShellHello, 20 EndpointControl).
- CAT-1862 ClientMessage::AttachTerminal: Switch connection into direct terminal attach by terminal_id; takeover=true replaces the existing writable attach owner.
- CAT-1864 ClientMessage::ControlTerminal: Writable control mode on a pane/terminal/agent target; takeover replaces existing controller.
- CAT-1873 ServerMessage enum: All server-to-client messages; variant order frozen for generation 1 (13 PaneSurface, 15 ClientShellError, 17 KeyboardReportAll, 18 EndpointResponseChunk, 19 PaneSurfacePatch, 20 EndpointControl).
- CAT-1875 ServerMessage::Terminal(TerminalFrame): Terminal ANSI bytes with per-client monotonic seq, size, and full-vs-diff flag.
- CAT-1890 ServerMessage::PaneSurface (PaneSurfaceFrame): Server-rendered active-tab surface without sidebar/tab bar/overlays: boot_id, projection_revision, surface_revision, FrameData, panes, splits, popup, graphics.
- CAT-1891 ServerMessage::PaneSurfacePatch: Incremental cell rows against base_surface_revision plus updated pane metadata and cursor.
- CAT-1895 ServerMessage::ClientShellEndpointResponseChunk: Ordered chunks (boot_id, request_id, final_chunk, data) forming the final response to an endpoint request.

### herdr / pty

- CAT-1897 Bounded command queue of 1024: ACTOR_COMMAND_BUFFER=1024 bounds the data channel; overflow yields Full/WouldBlock to callers.
- CAT-1904 nudge_child_redraw_after_handoff: After handoff, shrink by 1 row (or cols if rows<=2, min 4), sleep 30ms, restore real size to force child SIGWINCH redraw.
- CAT-1905 Nudge sleeps 30ms on actor thread: nudge() blocks the actor with thread::sleep(30ms) between the two resizes.
- CAT-1909 Closed actor returns BrokenPipe "pty actor closed": Submissions after exit/shutdown fail with BrokenPipe; queued ones fail "PTY actor closed during input submission".
- CAT-1910 Input silently dropped when not Running: WriteUserInput is discarded if state != Running (quiesced); SubmitUserInput gets BrokenPipe "not accepting input".
- CAT-1912 Partial/failed write clears queue and kills actor: A non-WouldBlock write error clears pending writes and exits the loop; WriteZero is an error.
- CAT-1913 Windows backend uses portable-pty MasterPty directly: On Windows SpawnedPty holds Box<dyn MasterPty>; no raw fd, no handoff, no foreground pgid, no poll loop.
- CAT-1916 Windows handle has no handoff or pgid methods: Windows handle lacks begin_handoff/duplicate_for_handoff/foreground_process_group_id methods present in unix.

### herdr / remote

- CAT-1921 bridge connects to the local socket per invocation: The bridge forwards one stream to the socket at `api::socket_path()` and fails with a path-bearing error if it is not listening.
- CAT-1923 is_remote_auth_error heuristics: Detects publickey, keyboard-interactive and password denial by substring on the ssh error text, then hints `ssh <target>` and `ssh-add`.
- CAT-1935 `--handoff` order not preserved when re-injected: The re-injected `--handoff` is appended at the end, after the other args, regardless of its original position.
- CAT-1938 no further target validation: Only emptiness and a leading dash are checked; whitespace, shell metacharacters and format are not validated here.
- CAT-1939 flag errors are plain strings: All errors are `Err(String)` with no codes or structured fields.
- CAT-1946 Supported remote platforms: POSIX remotes limited to linux/macos on x86_64/aarch64; Windows handled by separate PowerShell path (arm64 maps to x64 package per tests).
- CAT-1960 No SSH multiplexing off Unix: Without Unix multiplexing prepare_shared_transport returns false and interactive SSH recovery is unsupported; user must authenticate outside Herdr.
- CAT-1961 Noninteractive timeouts and output caps: Noninteractive commands time out at 15s, stderr capped 16 KiB, diagnostic output 256 KiB.
- CAT-1968 Restart prompts block headless runs: Without a TTY, a required upgrade or stop errors with "run from an interactive terminal to approve"; install of missing binary likewise requires a TTY.
- CAT-1969 stop_remote_server kills pane processes: Server stop terminates shells, agents, dev servers and tests; waits up to 5s polling every 100ms for shutdown; server restarts when a bridge attaches.
- CAT-1973 one SSH child per accepted connection: Each local connection spawns its own ssh process; connection end kills the child after 250ms drain.
- CAT-1976 local_forward_socket_path: Socket name embeds pid, sanitized target and session (readable name), with short-hash fallback to fit sun_path.
- CAT-1982 Unknown bridge options hard-fail: Any argument other than the empty list or `--idle-timeout-v1` returns "unsupported remote client bridge option".
- CAT-1984 Endpoint protocol generation gate: A listening server is accepted only if the status API capability `endpoint_protocol_generation` equals ENDPOINT_PROTOCOL_GENERATION.
- CAT-1988 Two client sockets: API vs client: The bridge connects to client_socket_path (attach stream) while status and registration use api::socket_path (JSON API).
- CAT-1995 endpoint_protocol_generation None = pre-floor server: A server that reports no generation is treated as outdated and needs an update.
- CAT-2004 API bridge socket path: Local socket named `herdr-api-ssh-<pid>-<profile_id>.sock`, with a short variant using a 16-char id prefix.
- CAT-2007 stale_metadata_failure string match: Detects a stale cache by searching the error text for STALE_API_METADATA.
- CAT-2009 saved_ssh_failure_needs_attention: Classifies failures as needing a user: InvalidInput, InvalidData, NotFound, PermissionDenied or Unsupported kinds, or messages such as permission denied, host key verification failed, "not ready", "install or update", protocol, handshake.
- CAT-2012 server.ssh_agent.register RPC: Request id `remote:ssh-agent`, method ServerSshAgentRegister with `socket_path`; the answer is `{"type":"ok"}`. The connection stays open and holds the registration.
- CAT-2015 Registration response capped at 4096 bytes, 500 ms: The register response must be a single newline-terminated line under 4096 bytes within 500 ms, or it fails with TimedOut.
- CAT-2016 Registration is unix only: The registration is started inside `#[cfg(unix)]`, and its tests use UnixListener.

### herdr / server

- CAT-2018 alt-screen read via synthetic wheel (PendingAltScreenRead): Deferred pane.read for panes on the alternate screen: server injects mouse-wheel scroll-up bytes into the live app, merges snapshots to reconstruct scrollback, scrolls back down, then answers over an mpsc<String> response channel.
- CAT-2019 alt-screen read time budgets: INITIAL/OUTPUT_QUIET 10 ms, STEP_TIMEOUT 120 ms per wheel step, MAX_DURATION 15 s traversal, MAX_RESTORE_DURATION 5 s; WHEEL_STEP_EVENTS=3 events per step.
- CAT-2021 fallback to passive snapshot: If the pane leaves the alternate screen, resizes, runtime vanishes, or wheel routing is not mouse-report, the read completes with the pre-built fallback_response instead of scrolled history.
- CAT-2022 wheel only when app enabled mouse reporting: send_wheel errors unless runtime.wheel_routing() == WheelRouting::MouseReport, targets the screen center cell, and repeats the encoded event N times in one write.
- CAT-2026 attach requires a usable terminal: auto_detect_launch rejects when platform::terminal_grid_size fails ("run inside a terminal") before touching sockets.
- CAT-2028 endpoint compatibility capabilities (endpoint_protocol_generation, surface_interest): Attach to a running server requires matching ENDPOINT_PROTOCOL_GENERATION; saved SSH machines additionally require surface_interest, else a "final server update" error with restart guidance.
- CAT-2032 reject_pending_client_connections during live handoff: Drains and drops queued connections so clients do not hang waiting for a Welcome that the old server will never send.
- CAT-2033 endpoint size limits: MAX_ENDPOINT_COMMAND_BYTES 1 MiB, MAX_ENDPOINT_BOOT_ID_BYTES 128, MAX_ENDPOINT_REQUEST_ID_BYTES 128; response chunk size 512 KiB.
- CAT-2039 chunked deferred responses and server_unavailable: spawn_response_waiter waits on a std mpsc receiver, emits server_unavailable if the sender dropped, and splits payload into 512 KiB chunks with final_chunk on last.
- CAT-2054 handshake timeout 4 s: HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT closes connections that do not send a hello in 4 s (chosen to stay under a 5 s deadline).
- CAT-2055 input payload and batch limits: MAX_INPUT_PAYLOAD 1 MiB per input message; MAX_INPUT_EVENT_BATCH 4096 expanded events.
- CAT-2059 two-lane client writer (control vs droppable render): ClientWriter has a reliable control queue and a render slot of capacity one; slow clients drop frames rather than accumulate lag; discard_pending_render clears it.
- CAT-2061 ServerEvent::ClientAttachTerminal (takeover): Direct attach to one terminal_id with a takeover boolean.
- CAT-2064 pane input limit classification: pane_input_event_limit expands Key repeat_count and scroll lines; too many events or non-paste payload overflow closes the connection, paste-only overflow is rejected without closing.
- CAT-2066 legacy ClientShellHello and non-handshake first message rejected: ClientShellHello gets Welcome error "upgrade the Herdr client"; any other first message gets "expected TerminalHello or ClientShellHello" then close.
- CAT-2067 read-loop framing size caps: Handshake read uses MAX_FRAME_SIZE; post-handshake reads allow MAX_GRAPHICS_FRAME_SIZE; oversize or read error closes the connection after emitting ClientDisconnected.
- CAT-2068 observer socket becomes non-blocking with 30 s send timeout: On ObserveTerminal (unix) the stream gets set_send_timeout(30 s) and nonblocking; failure shuts the connection.
- CAT-2072 ClientConnection.last_activity: Monotonic stamp; the most recently active shell client becomes the foreground client that drives PTY size and host side effects.
- CAT-2073 latest_shell_client: Picks the active shell client with max last_activity as fallback foreground.
- CAT-2076 DeferredRender / render_pending: If the per-client render channel is full an ordinary render is skipped and a Full re-render is deferred rather than queued.
- CAT-2077 ClientConnection.shell_endpoint_command_in_flight: A shell has at most one ordered endpoint command in flight; deferred navigation runs only if the same surface lease is still active.
- CAT-2081 Server already running: If API or client socket bind returns AddrInUse the server prints "herdr server is already running" with the socket path and exits 1.
- CAT-2085 Live handoff Unix only: Non-Unix builds return "live handoff is only supported on Unix".
- CAT-2088 handoff version/protocol gates: Import fails if manifest.version != 1, expected_protocol differs from PROTOCOL_VERSION, or expected_version differs from build version.
- CAT-2089 MAX_REPLAY_BYTES_PER_PANE: Handoff replays at most 8 KiB of recent output per pane so the new server repaints.
- CAT-2092 headless_size / effective_size: Virtual terminal size is the configured headless size with no clients; with clients, the foreground client dictates the shared pane runtime size.
- CAT-2093 tab_geometry_controllers: Ephemeral shell connection controls PTY geometry per stable tab id.
- CAT-2096 server_unavailable during shutdown: While shutting_down or a host shutdown is announced, API requests are rejected with server_unavailable; queued ones drained likewise.
- CAT-2100 agent_not_idle read error: agent.read with lines on a known non-idle agent in alternate screen and short visible history returns agent_not_idle; history only captured by scrolling while idle; suggests --source visible.
- CAT-2101 AltScreenReadSpec / deferred alt-screen reads: For idle known agents in an alternate screen with mouse-report wheel routing, history reads are done by scrolling the viewport; concurrent text reads get a frozen snapshot, other formats are deferred; lines default 80 and cap 1000.
- CAT-2106 terminal attach exclusivity and --takeover: One writable attach owner per terminal; a second gets "already has an attached client; retry with --takeover"; takeover sends "terminal attach taken over" to the previous owner and disconnects it.
- CAT-2107 attach locks resize: Attach adds the terminal to direct_attach_resize_locks, resumes pending agent, and resizes the runtime to the attached client size.
- CAT-2108 ServerMessage::ServerShutdown{reason}: Used for errors, takeover, handoff ("live update in progress; reconnect after handoff completes") and shutdown; the only error channel for terminal-mode clients.
- CAT-2109 ignore_client_event_during_handoff: During handoff all client events except connect/disconnect/writer-drain/quit are ignored; connects are rejected.
- CAT-2111 paste size limit: Oversized input messages rejected with ClientPasteRejected{size,max}; shells get ClientShellError, terminal clients a Toast Notify.
- CAT-2113 ClientResize / ClientShellResize: Client resize updates terminal_size and cell pixel size; attach clients resize the runtime; shell resize records the surface size.
- CAT-2118 promote_client_to_foreground: Sets foreground client and syncs host state; removing the foreground client promotes the latest remaining one.
- CAT-2119 send_to_client write semantics: Frames ServerMessage (with max size) and queues on the client writer; a detached client with no writer returns success without queuing.
- CAT-2121 reject_late_client_connections: During shutdown new connections are rejected.
- CAT-2123 error endpoint_busy: Only one shell-lane command may be in flight per client; a second gets endpoint_busy.
- CAT-2124 error surface_inactive: Any shell-lane command except surface.set is refused until the client has an active surface lease.
- CAT-2128 handoff disconnects all clients: disconnect_all_clients_for_handoff and reject_pending_client_connections run before commit; every attached client and new connection is dropped.
- CAT-2131 live handoff unsupported off Unix: Non-unix build returns the error "live handoff is only supported on Unix".
- CAT-2135 geometry controller per tab: tab_geometry_controllers maps tab_id to one client; only that client size drives pane PTY size for the tab (claim_shell_tab_geometry, claim_unowned..., resize_shell_tab_if_controller); with one active client all tabs resize to it.
- CAT-2137 ServerMessage::GraphicsFile: Sends the client a server-local file path, expected_len, image_id, transfer_id and kitty control string (a=t,f=32,...) so the client reads decoded pixels from disk instead of the socket.
- CAT-2138 native graphics disabled per client after failure: A failed or timed-out native transfer inserts the client into disabled and sends GraphicsTransmissionRetired; native graphics stay off for that connection and inline assets are used.
- CAT-2139 ServerMessage::GraphicsTransmissionRetired: Tells the client to permanently reject a native transfer (transfer_id, image_id), including a file still in its render queue.
- CAT-2145 NotificationShowReason (Shown, Disabled, NoForegroundClient, RateLimited): notification.show returns a success result with shown:false and a reason instead of an error when disabled, no shell client is attached, or rate limited; empty title returns invalid_params.
- CAT-2146 notifications go to foreground client only: Bell, clipboard (base64 ServerMessage::Clipboard) and sound/toast Notify are sent only to the foreground client; without one they are dropped with a debug log.
- CAT-2151 no clients means no frames: With no render targets render_and_stream only recomputes view geometry and returns; attach streams exist only while a client is connected.
- CAT-2152 PaneSurfaceFrame: Full-frame message for shell clients: boot_id, projection_revision, surface_revision, cell frame, panes (rects, focus, scroll), splits, popup, graphics.
- CAT-2154 synchronized output defers frames: Frames are withheld while a pane has DEC 2026 synchronized output active and recomputed after; attach render rechecks the epoch to avoid tearing.
- CAT-2155 frame size caps: Frames use protocol::MAX_FRAME_SIZE, or MAX_GRAPHICS_FRAME_SIZE with graphics; oversized frames trim inline graphics assets one at a time, otherwise the frame is skipped.
- CAT-2160 shutdown stops API drain immediately: When should_quit is set, drain_api_requests_with_shutdown_check processes nothing and leaves queued requests unanswered in the batch (they are rejected later in complete_shutdown).
- CAT-2168 endpoint request error removes client: A terminal client whose endpoint request errors is dropped from the server.
- CAT-2171 synchronized output holds frame: Pane frames wait for synchronized output (DEC 2026) completion before commit, including for popups and siblings; hidden zoomed panes do not block.
- CAT-2173 client-local tab focus: Tab focus changes affect only the source connection; each client keeps own navigation.
- CAT-2174 pane_focused only when client moves: Client-local navigation emits pane_focused only when that client moves; no global focus transitions.
- CAT-2180 terminal attach rejects missing terminal: ClientAttachTerminal for unknown terminal removes the client; direct attach resize locks restore shell pane size on disconnect.
- CAT-2181 synchronized output observers wait: Terminal observers wait for synchronized output with or without baseline.
- CAT-2182 agent_not_idle error on alt-screen history read: agent.read with lines on alt-screen while working returns agent_not_idle; default lines or source visible are allowed.
- CAT-2183 alt-screen history only while idle: Alt-screen history is captured by scrolling, only possible when agent is idle; pending_alt_screen_reads queue.
- CAT-2187 second controller rejected without takeover: Second controller is rejected and its connection dropped unless takeover true.
- CAT-2188 takeover replaces controller: takeover true disconnects the existing controller (client 7 removed).
- CAT-2190 observe/attach mode exclusivity: Attach after observe (and observe after attach) is rejected, client removed, ownership cleared.
- CAT-2192 Windows shutdown probe: Platform-specific shutdown path tested separately for Windows.
- CAT-2201 clipboard write foreground only: Clipboard write to foreground client only; failed send removes client; no foreground means no visual change.
- CAT-2203 oversized paste rejection: Oversized paste rejected, notifying only sender.
- CAT-2205 notification.show reason no_foreground_client: Returns shown false with reason NoForegroundClient when none attached.
- CAT-2212 client_accept and handoff are #[cfg(unix)] only: Client accept loop and live server handoff compile only on unix; no equivalent on other platforms.
- CAT-2221 derive_client_socket_from_api_socket: Client socket = <api stem>-client.sock in same dir (herdr.sock -> herdr-client.sock; no extension -> custom-api-client.sock). Two sockets: JSON API and client protocol.
- CAT-2224 apply_scroll routing (WheelRouting): Wheel routes by child mode: MouseReport -> encoded mouse wheel bytes; AlternateScroll -> arrow-style bytes; HostScroll/None -> host scrollback scroll_up/down. PageKey scrolls host scrollback only when plain_page_keys_use_host_scrollback.
- CAT-2226 scroll_reset on any input: Any key/text/paste/button input snaps the pane out of scrollback before sending; mouse Moved does not reset.
- CAT-2228 non-pane input rejected: Raw events Mouse, OuterFocus*, HostDefaultColor, HostPaletteColors, HostColorSchemeChanged, HostCellSizeReport, Unsupported reaching targeted pane input return Err "non-pane input reached targeted pane input".
- CAT-2232 enable_surface_reuse / surface_delta / surface_scroll capability flags: Per-client opt-in compression of surface updates (reuse, delta, scroll); legacy peers without negotiation get plain PaneSurface/PaneSurfacePatch.
- CAT-2233 TerminalFrame {seq,width,height,full,bytes}: TerminalAnsi mode emits ServerMessage::Terminal with monotonically increasing seq, full flag and ANSI bytes; skips frame if encoder is current; graphics bytes spliced before final sync-end.
- CAT-2235 prepare_pane_surface_patch precondition: Patch only if boot_id, projection_revision and base_surface_revision match last committed surface and no recompute pending; otherwise None (caller sends full surface).
- CAT-2237 pop_pane_surface_asset largest-first trimming: When frame too large, drop largest inline graphics asset first, keeping placement metadata; delta/reuse messages return None so baseline is invalidated and a full surface retried.
- CAT-2241 ServerEvent::ClientShellConnected fields: Connect carries surface_reuse, surface_delta, surface_scroll, client_id, surface cols/rows, cell px size, pixel_mouse, direct_graphics, endpoint_keybindings, mouse_capture, surface_active, writer.
- CAT-2243 background surface activation preserves focused viewer geometry: Per-tab geometry controller is the focused client; a background client activating does not resize the shared pane.
- CAT-2244 focused surface reassertion reclaims tab geometry: Re-sending focus/active request returns tab geometry control to that client.
- CAT-2246 surface_scroll EndpointControl message: With surface_scroll negotiated, scrolling output is sent as EndpointControl kind surface_scroll::MESSAGE_KIND (shift + new rows), expanding to a PaneSurfacePatch via Decoder; more than 4x smaller than raw rows.
- CAT-2247 native graphics tokens: Started then Result: Native file export transfers need a Started ack with NATIVE_TRANSFER_BIT token before Result success counts; early success or old API tokens are ignored.
- CAT-2248 native timeout falls back inline on control lane: On expiry retirement goes over control lane (not blocked by full render lane), file unlinked, native disabled for that client, full inline render deferred.
- CAT-2249 native source files (FileStore::native_sources): Source-backed images are exported as files in a source directory (e.g. producer.rgba); path reused across upload, file released when last Arc owner drops; snapshotted source survives producer unlink (linux).
- CAT-2251 offscreen image retention bounded (LRU): Offscreen terminal images stay loaded until deleted; least recently visible evicted when over capacity (test uses 17 ids).

### herdr / terminal

- CAT-2261 Handoff is unix-only: Every handoff method is cfg(unix); no handoff on other platforms
- CAT-2275 Read is snapshot, not stream: Every read method returns a point-in-time copy; truth for live output is the PTY/attach stream
- CAT-2277 Snapshot can fail under write load: screen_text_snapshot_with_seq gives up after 3 attempts and returns None
- CAT-2289 try_send_bytes: Non-blocking send of raw bytes to the PTY via bounded mpsc; returns TrySendError when full
- CAT-2300 Ambiguous alignment rejected: upward_alignment returns None when two shifts are plausible, so history is left unchanged
- CAT-2319 Handoff snapshot only for full-lifecycle authority: `handoff_agent_state` returns None unless the hook authority is a live full-lifecycle one, so fallback-detected or custom state is rebuilt by re-detection after handoff.
- CAT-2320 route_full_lifecycle_hook_report: Decides whether a lifecycle hook report is accepted, ignored, or buffered. It rejects stale sessions and OpenCode cross-talk. After process exit it buffers reports until fresh process evidence arrives; a buffered report needs both a session_ref and a seq.
- CAT-2345 set_hook_authority_with_session_ref / set_hook_authority_at: Entry point for an agent hook report (source, agent_label, state, message, session_ref, seq). It returns None when the report is ignored; there is no error reason.
- CAT-2346 Non-full-lifecycle report ignored after process exit: A custom (non-full-lifecycle) hook for an agent whose process recently exited is dropped.
- CAT-2348 Unsequenced report ignored once source uses seq: Mixing sequenced and unsequenced reports from one source drops the unsequenced ones.
- CAT-2355 session_report_allows_session_replacement table: Hard-coded allowlist of which session-start sources replace an existing session ref per agent: claude, codex, mastracode, hermes, opencode, pi, grok, omp, qwen, antigravity_cli (agy). This is per-agent integration policy compiled in, not user config.
- CAT-2364 Managed launch timeout silently releases name: If the deadline passes before Idle, the agent name is cleared with no error surfaced here.
- CAT-2369 Process-exit clears hook, session, resume, metadata: On exit, matching hook authority, persisted session, reported resume, and agent metadata (sources and sequences) are removed. A newer custom authority (`reported_at > now`) is preserved.
- CAT-2374 Strip exactly one glyph: After removing one recognized glyph it trims the rest and does not strip again ("⠋ ⠙ task" gives "⠙ task").
- CAT-2376 Only mid-title and unrecognized symbols preserved: Unrecognized leading symbols, mid-title glyphs and bracketed prefixes are left untouched ("task ⠋ detail", "[prod] task", "@ task").
- CAT-2377 Title cleanup is Claude-Code-shaped: The glyph set is named for Claude Code, so other agents (Codex, pi, OmO) with different title conventions are not normalized.
- CAT-2378 pub(crate) visibility, no external surface: The function is crate-private; no RPC, config key or CLI flag exposes or toggles the stripping.

### herdr / ui

- CAT-2379 resize_background_tab_panes: Resizes panes in every non-active tab of every workspace to the current area, so hidden agents see the viewport size too.
- CAT-2386 release_notes_preview_line_entries: Preview mode shows "update ready" plus an install instruction from crate::update::update_install_instruction (test shows: detach, run herdr update, then run Herdr again to reconnect).
- CAT-2399 compute_tab_surface: Layout for the active workspace and its active tab; optionally resizes pane PTYs; takes host cell pixel size.
- CAT-2400 resize_tab_surface: Resizes all runtimes of a given tab to the geometry they would get if selected (resizes background tabs too).
- CAT-2402 tab_surface_cursor: Computes the host cursor (x,y,visible,shape) of the focused pane; None when pane does not expose host cursor, synchronized output is active, or pane is scrolled back.
- CAT-2405 pane_is_scrolled_back: A pane is scrolled back when ScrollMetrics.offset_from_bottom > 0; hides the cursor.
- CAT-2407 terminal_inner_rect scrollbar gutter: Scrollbar gutter column (1 col) reserved on primary screen when pane_scrollbars on and width>4; reclaimed on alternate screen; reserved even before scrollback exists.
- CAT-2411 MIN_PANE_ROWS / MIN_PANE_COLS clamp: New terminal sizes are clamped up to crate::pane::MIN_PANE_ROWS/MIN_PANE_COLS.
- CAT-2412 resize_tab_panes: Resizes every runtime in a tab (zoomed: only the focused pane) using chrome-adjusted inner rect and host cell pixel size.
- CAT-2413 direct_attach_resize_locks: Terminals in app.direct_attach_resize_locks are skipped when resizing, so a direct-attached client keeps control of PTY size.
- CAT-2415 render_panes restore failure display: If a pane has no runtime but its terminal has restore_error, the error text is painted in the pane instead of a terminal.
- CAT-2418 render_tab_surface_virtual (test reference): Test renders via crate::server::render_stream::render_tab_surface_virtual(app, runtimes, layout, area) returning buffer and cursor, showing the server renders a virtual buffer for streamed clients.

### herdr / workspace

- CAT-2426 NEXT_WORKSPACE_ID counter: Id counter is process-global in-memory (starts at 1); only restored workspaces re-seed it, so ids are not unique across independent sessions/servers.
- CAT-2438 close_focused: Closes the focused pane; returns true when the whole workspace should close (last pane of last tab).
- CAT-2450 tab_idx is vector index not public tab number: Test pins that PaneDetail.tab_idx is the Vec index, not the stable user-facing Tab.number.
- CAT-2462 Last pane cannot be closed via detach_pane: detach_pane returns None when pane_count <= 1; the tab itself must be closed by the caller.
- CAT-2467 Tab::foreground_cwd_for_pane: Cwd of the pane foreground process only from the live runtime; no stored fallback.
- CAT-2471 Reftable support requires git binary: git_ref_storage_is_reftable routes to git symbolic-ref/rev-parse subprocesses via noninteractive_process.
- CAT-2478 Non-git cwd negative cache of 30 s: A cwd outside any repo caches a miss with retry_after = now+30s and skips filesystem rechecks.
- CAT-2479 Ahead/behind only from local refs: ahead_behind runs git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...upstream on local objects; no fetch, no dirty/untracked info.

### herdr / root files

- CAT-2485 validate_resume_argv: Rejects empty argv, >64 args, >8192 total bytes, control chars, apostrophes, and any first element that is not a plain command name (alnum/_/-/.; no leading -, no path).
- CAT-2486 Restore types the command into the pane shell: Resume works by typing a quoted argv into the pane shell (POSIX quoting), hence the apostrophe and bare-command restrictions.
- CAT-2492 is_official_agent_source allowlist: Only herdr:<agent> source names paired with matching agent (18 agents incl. antigravity_cli/agy) are accepted; custom sources are rejected for session refs.
- CAT-2512 Handoff drops transient coordination: In-flight requests, waits, subscriptions, client sockets, pane-to-pane messages are not preserved; clients must reconnect and retry.
- CAT-2513 Handoff is unix-only: HandoffRuntimeState and the master_fd are cfg(unix); no handoff on Windows.
- CAT-2524 close_focused returns focus to prev_focus: Closing the focused pane focuses `prev_focus` if still open; otherwise the next pane in order, else the previous one. The last pane can never be closed (returns false).
- CAT-2526 focus_pane: Sets focus to a pane if it exists; silently ignores unknown ids.
- CAT-2531 Rotating log files in data_dir: Logs go to the session data dir via `RotatingFileMakeWriter`, max 5 MiB, 0 retained rotations. Logging is silently skipped if the writer fails.
- CAT-2532 DEFAULT_RETAINED_LOG_FILES = 0: No rotated copies are retained, so earlier logs are discarded at rotation.
- CAT-2540 MetadataTokens::values: Returns a snapshot map of key -> value without mutating, even for expired-but-not-swept entries.
- CAT-2543 MAX_SEQUENCE_SOURCES = 32: Tracking is bounded to 32 distinct sources; a 33rd new source gets `Err(())`, while existing sources keep working.
- CAT-2544 curl_command helper: Shells out to the system `curl` binary, used for update and version checks.
- CAT-2546 Nested herdr blocked by default: Launching herdr in a pane with `HERDR_ENV=1` exits 1 unless `[experimental] allow_nested = true`. Applies to the default launch and to hidden `client` mode.
- CAT-2550 --remote restricted to default launch: `--remote` combined with any subcommand is an error (exit 2), except with help, version, default-config or skill.
- CAT-2558 Strict unknown flag and command rejection: Unknown `-` flags and unknown positional commands exit 2. The positional allow-list names: server, client, remote-client-bridge, update, status, config, channel, machine, workspace, worktree, pane, session, integration.
- CAT-2560 [server] keys: `headless_cols` (120) and `headless_rows` (40) set the virtual terminal size when no client is attached. Windows-only `allow_unelevated_clients`.
- CAT-2582 flush timeouts (10, 150, 50, 500, 500 ms): Idle flush is 10 ms. Mouse-active escape flush is 150 ms, CSI introducer 50 ms, disambiguated mouse tail 500 ms, incomplete sequence 500 ms.
- CAT-2585 host reply windows: A 1 s quiet window treats `ESC[` and `ESC]` as possible host replies rather than keys, and an unfinished OSC 10/11 reply is dropped after 1 s.
- CAT-2593 Windows keyboard protocol no-op: On Windows the kitty keyboard and direct keyboard protocol functions write nothing, only record state.
- CAT-2614 One-shot stop connection: stop opens a fresh connection, writes one request, reads a single line and drops it; server closes after answering.
- CAT-2615 Stopping exits pane processes: Update guidance states "Stopping exits pane processes" and instructs stop then re-attach with the same socket override.
- CAT-2618 Self-update disabled for managed installs: Homebrew, mise and Nix installs refuse self-update and print their own upgrade command; preview channel unsupported there.
- CAT-2619 running_inside_herdr guard: `herdr update` refuses to run inside a herdr pane (HERDR_ENV marker) and tells the user to detach first.
- CAT-2623 send_server_update_method_at: Sends one-line JSON {id, method} request over the local socket with send/recv timeouts, reads one line, treats any "error" field as failure.
- CAT-2626 Handoff timeouts: Server handoff request timeout 240s, confirm timeout 30s, stop response 5s, shutdown poll 100ms.
- CAT-2631 Windows update path: Windows uses embedded PowerShell installer (distribution/install.ps1); no live handoff or server management; running servers stay active.
- CAT-2637 expand_tilde_absolute_path: Tilde-expands, then makes relative paths absolute against the server's current working directory.
- CAT-2643 is_dirty_worktree_remove_error: Classifies git stderr as "needs force" when it contains "contains modified or untracked files" plus "use --force to delete it", or "working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed". Locked-worktree messages are deliberately not matched.
- CAT-2644 is_not_working_tree_remove_error: Detects "is not a working tree" / "is not a worktree" removal errors, which trigger forced recovery.
- CAT-2645 worktree_dirty_remove_message (windows): Windows-only synthesized message mimicking git's dirty-remove error. Implies that on Windows herdr pre-checks dirtiness itself instead of relying on git's refusal.
- CAT-2649 run_worktree_add_command: Chooses existing-branch vs new-branch add automatically, then runs it. The `base` argument is ignored when the branch already exists.
- CAT-2650 run_worktree_command: Runs git with `LC_ALL=C`, collects output, returns Err(String) with stderr, else stdout, else "git failed with status".
- CAT-2655 list_existing_worktrees is synchronous: Spawns git and blocks the calling thread with no timeout. Callers must run it off the server loop (see test_list_gate message).

### herdr / herdr docs website

- CAT-2663 Current pane resolution: `--current` resolves `HERDR_PANE_ID` inside a pane; otherwise commands may use focused pane, while explicit `--current` errors if caller pane identity is absent.
- CAT-2664 Pane move identity: Cross-workspace moves change workspace-qualified pane ID; use returned new ID, while prior ID remains an alias and process launch-time environment IDs remain unchanged.
- CAT-2666 Snapshot reads: `pane read` and `agent read` return snapshots; recent sources default to 80 rendered rows, while visible/detection default to full snapshots.
- CAT-2669 Indefinite waits and ambiguous delivery: Waits have no default timeout; timeout or stalled prompt does not prove input was not delivered, so inspect before retrying.
- CAT-2672 Agent readiness and timeout: Start waits for ready/idle, blocked startup returns `agent_not_ready`; prompt blocked returns `agent_blocked`, and non-working prompt wait requires observed activity or returns `agent_prompt_stalled`.
- CAT-2673 Completion and seen state: `done` means idle but unseen; focus marks it seen, reads do not, and each TUI client tracks viewed completions independently.
- CAT-2674 Unknown and blocked detection: Screen detection uses live bottom-buffer manifests; unmatched known agents fall back to idle, and unusual prompts may be misclassified, so inspect before interacting.
- CAT-2678 Resume argv constraints: Resume argv starts with a plain PATH command, has at most 64 arguments and 8 KiB total, and excludes apostrophes/control characters; source must first hold pane or receives `resume_not_accepted`.
- CAT-2685 Metadata bounds: Metadata normalizes text, limits values to 80 characters, TTL to 1–86,400,000 ms, and accepts sequenced token reports from at most 32 sources per pane/workspace lifetime.
- CAT-2686 Alternate-screen history: For idle recognized agents, recent reads requesting more than visible rows can use mouse scrolling to collect overlapping transcript pages and return viewport to bottom.
- CAT-2688 Terminal controller ownership: One controller owns a terminal; `--takeover` replaces it. Observers are read-only and multiple observers may coexist; stalled observer writes may close without a final closed record.
- CAT-2690 Remote API forwarding: Requests travel as JSON over non-interactive SSH without shell interpolation; forwarding does not install/start/restart servers, retry failures, or fall back to Local.
- CAT-2692 Cached disconnected state: Disconnected machine rows show dimmed cached workspace/agent state; input and navigation are disabled until a new connection and corresponding screen arrive.
- CAT-2696 TUI-only confirmation: CLI/API closes are immediate; configured close confirmation applies to TUI keybindings and menus, while grouped workspace close can require explicit `--group`.
- CAT-2697 Plugin install trust: GitHub plugin installs use Git, show an interactive trust preview, may run supported build commands, and require `--yes` non-interactively.
- CAT-2698 Plugin popup boundary: Popup plugin commands are not Herdr panes, export no `HERDR_PANE_ID`, and do not participate in pane/agent APIs.
- CAT-2701 Update server behavior: Default update replaces client binary while keeping compatible running server and panes; new server features need server restart, while experimental `--handoff` is opt-in.
- CAT-2703 Windows and platform constraints: SSH auth recovery is not supported on local Windows; supported remote server architectures and several terminal features vary by platform.
- CAT-2706 Pane move changes pane ID: Moving panes across workspaces changes the prefixed ID; use `move_result.pane.pane_id`, and in-flight waits may end `agent_not_running`.
- CAT-2710 Prompt retry ambiguity: Timeout or `agent_prompt_stalled` does not prove no input was sent; read agent state/output before retrying.
- CAT-2711 Waits have no default timeout: Agent and pane wait commands may wait indefinitely unless callers supply timeouts.
- CAT-2722 Event history loss: Event history is nondurable; lagging subscribers receive `events_lost` and their subscription connection closes.
- CAT-2723 Event subscription validation: If any subscription references a nonexistent pane, the whole request is rejected and the connection closed.
- CAT-2729 No plugin storage API: Plugin v1 provides no Herdr-managed storage API; plugins must manage files in discovered config/state directories.
- CAT-2730 Session snapshot recovery: Herdr preserves failed-load recovery copies and layout snapshots, but does not restore them automatically.
- CAT-2732 Handoff interrupts coordination: Live handoff preserves PTYs/processes and durable state, but in-flight requests, waits, streams, sockets, and pane messages may be interrupted.
- CAT-2733 Windows direct attach: `herdr terminal attach`, live server handoff, Unix descriptor handoff/process groups, and local native-pane clipboard image bridge are unsupported on Windows.
- CAT-2734 Remote SSH attach: `herdr --remote <target>` attaches to remote sessions; Windows OpenSSH lacks Herdr's Unix control-socket reuse, so ssh-agent is recommended.
- CAT-2737 Windows integration coverage: Windows supports a narrower set of agent integrations; unsupported install formats are hidden or rejected.
- CAT-2739 Binary protocol build compatibility: Numbered binary protocol operations remain same-install/internal; check `ping` or status before cross-build direct attach or handoff.
- CAT-2744 Agent wait is semantic: `agent wait` and `agent prompt --wait` observe agent state, not completion of background tasks or subprocesses.
- CAT-2745 `HERDR_PROCESS_DETECTION`: Opts the server into child-process-group inference when native foreground process detection is unavailable.
- CAT-2755 Remote commands do not fall back or retry: Authentication, connection, and version errors do not fall back to Local; failed requests are not automatically retried.
- CAT-2765 Stable agent target: Agent target is a unique live agent name or its current pane ID; terminal IDs and kind labels are invalid.
- CAT-2769 `ui.confirm_close`: Requires TUI confirmation for certain last-tab or unique-pane close actions; CLI/API close remains immediate.
- CAT-2771 Machine-scoped identifiers: Workspace, tab, pane IDs, and agent names are valid only on their owning server.
- CAT-2773 Snapshot restore: Server restart restores workspace, tab, pane, cwd, layout, and focus state, but not arbitrary running processes.
- CAT-2778 Handoff interrupts transient coordination: In-flight requests, waits, subscriptions, client sockets, and pane messages may be interrupted; clients should reconnect and retry.
- CAT-2779 Exclusive attachment ownership: One writable direct-attach client owns terminal input and resize; `--takeover` replaces the current owner.
- CAT-2789 Event subscription validation: Every subscription entry must be valid; one missing pane rejects the whole request and closes the connection.
- CAT-2790 Bounded event history: Event history is not persistent; lag beyond retention returns `events_lost` and closes that subscription connection.
- CAT-2792 Snapshot/event ordering: Snapshot and events have no shared sequence boundary; do not blindly replay buffered event payloads over a snapshot.
- CAT-2794 `workspace.metadata_updated`: Reports workspace token changes and TTL expiration to API subscribers but does not invoke plugin event hooks.
- CAT-2796 Public socket graphics API removed: `pane.graphics.info/set/clear/stream` are unavailable and no replacement socket image API exists.
- CAT-2798 Plugin execution authority: Plugins are not sandboxed or behavior-reviewed by Herdr and run with the user's available authority.
- CAT-2804 Plugin storage API absent: Plugins own their state files, schemas, migrations, and cleanup; Herdr v1 only exposes config/state directory paths.
- CAT-2806 `server.allow_unelevated_clients`: Windows-only opt-in permits ordinary processes of the same account to control an elevated server's panes.
- CAT-2807 Windows unsupported capabilities: Windows does not support direct terminal attach, live server handoff, Unix FD handoff, Unix foreground process groups, or local native-pane clipboard image bridge.

### herdr / herdr api schema

- CAT-2820 server.ssh_agent.register: Registers an absolute remote-host agent socket; registration lasts until the API connection closes.
- CAT-2850 agent.send_keys: Sends key input to an agent target.

### herdr / herdr AGENTS/skills

- CAT-2936 Move pane ID replacement: Moving a pane across workspaces gives it a new qualified ID; callers should use move_result pane ID or live agent name.
- CAT-2941 Machine API forwarding: Remote forwarding requires compatible running servers and never installs, starts, restarts, or falls back to Local.
- CAT-2943 SSH reconnect authentication: `machine reconnect` requires the user to complete SSH authentication in their terminal.
- CAT-2949 Lifecycle wait scope: Agent waits track lifecycle state, not an individual turn; an already-running turn may satisfy completion wait.
- CAT-2953 Command admission is not execution: `pane run` success acknowledges admission only; it does not prove the command ran.
- CAT-2956 Pane snapshot and scrollback: Reads can request screen/host-scrollback rows, but alternate-screen rows are excluded and application history is not always recoverable.
- CAT-2970 Named-session shared config: Named sessions isolate runtime state, sockets, panes, and persistence, but share global config and manifest overrides by default.
- CAT-3002 Keybinding configuration: The prefix defaults to `ctrl+b`; `prefix+?` displays active bindings and every binding, including prefix, is configurable under `[keys]`.
- CAT-3009 API details not in scoped files: The guide points to a socket API reference but documents no RPC method names, request/response schema, event protocol, or connection lifetime here.
- CAT-3010 Restart/update survival unspecified: The guide links to session-state documentation rather than detailing what survives restart or update in this file.

### herdr / herdr agent-detection tomls

- CAT-3015 Unknown overlays preserve state: `skip_state_update = true` marks transcript viewers, model pickers, and menus as unknown without applying a state update.
- CAT-3016 Conservative no-evidence fallback: Letta's final catch-all rule reports unknown because there is no live-state evidence.
- CAT-3022 Background tasks may not mean working: Antigravity notes background tasks/subagents stop counting as working once the agent returns to its prompt.
- CAT-3023 Do not infer work from retained rows: Grok notes background commands, monitors, and subagents left running after return to prompt do not count as working.
- CAT-3024 Prompt presence is not activity: Qwen keeps its composer visible while responding, so prompt-box presence alone is not idle evidence.
- CAT-3026 Progress support varies: Qwen emits OSC 9;4 only during tool execution and only when the terminal advertises progress support.
- CAT-3027 Agent UI variations require fallbacks: Rules account for legacy dialogs, narrow panes, hidden/remapped interrupt hints, locales, and alternate spinner styles.

### herdr-core / src

- CAT-3035 attach frame kinds: Attach channel carries DATA, CREDIT (output flow control by payload length), CLOSE (with end reason JSON), FACTS (display JSON), FOCUS (1 byte) and RESIZE (cols,rows u32 LE).
- CAT-3037 socket mismatch detection: If core.lock names another live socket than the one this env resolves, returns unavailable explaining XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or HC_SOCKET differ.
- CAT-3038 one plain call: Writes one JSON-RPC request line (id 1) and reads one reply line, then the caller drops the stream; errors map to RpcError or unavailable.
- CAT-3039 closed-connection recovery hint: If the core closes mid-call, waits up to 10 s for a core to reappear and reports restart vs stop with a rerun hint.
- CAT-3045 plain subscriber queue: A plain-mode subscriber may queue 1024 events before it is counted as behind.
- CAT-3053 exec output caps: stdout kept up to 8 MiB, stderr 1 MiB, stdin up to 8 MiB; excess dropped and `truncated` set.
- CAT-3055 exec concurrency cap: At most 16 execs run at once; more get error unavailable.
- CAT-3059 exec cwd resolution: cwd relative to the core folder, or to HOME for a caller from afar.
- CAT-3061 file transfer caps: One read returns or one write takes at most 8 MB; files over 64 MB are rejected for read/edit.
- CAT-3062 text-only files: Only regular UTF-8 files; pipes, devices give invalid_params; non-UTF-8 gives not_text hint to use exec cat.
- CAT-3067 foreground per OS: Linux via /proc, macOS via sysctl, Windows via PEB reads on the first process (no foreground group) and None for 32-bit processes.
- CAT-3075 human typing gate: Human keys while an agent input is going are held and delivered afterward; agent input waits until the person has been quiet (default 3 s, HC_QUIET_MS).
- CAT-3077 startup settle wait: In the first 10 s a send waits up to 5 s for output to be still for 800 ms (HC_SETTLE_MS), else error unavailable with nothing typed.
- CAT-3082 kept recovery: Lost kept terminals get a fresh own-shell terminal id retained, state reset (template, title, submit, stop cleared), cwd last known folder; skipped while stopping or host shutdown.
- CAT-3084 no plus key: The plus key itself cannot be named (ctrl++ unsupported); F13+ unsupported.
- CAT-3086 remote pipe: Remote core reached by `ssh <target> herdr-core connect` with BatchMode, ConnectTimeout 10, keepalives; never prompts; session via HC_SESSION; Windows lines handled.
- CAT-3090 message tags: Agent-to-agent text wrapped as `<hc from="t3 name">text</hc>` (with reach hint for first message) when both report status.
- CAT-3099 put::MAX_BYTES: One terminal.put carries at most 8 MiB raw bytes, inline base64 in a single message.
- CAT-3102 Relay (output filter): Every program byte reaches the core screen; viewers get every byte except queries (CSI c/n/p/q/t/u, OSC with ?, DCS $q/+q) that the screen answered itself, so a query is answered exactly once.
- CAT-3103 APC / kitty graphics handling: The screen consumes APC graphics (cursor moves) but its replies are dropped; only a viewer able to show images answers.
- CAT-3111 plain vs framed connection: A connection starts plain (one JSON-RPC message per line); a successful `hello` with framed:true switches to binary frames (channel 0 = JSON-RPC, other channels = streams).
- CAT-3112 plain events.subscribe stream: After events.subscribe on a plain connection it carries notification lines only; further lines the client sends are read and ignored; ends on close.
- CAT-3115 framed frame kinds: Framed loop handles DATA (channel 0 JSON-RPC, others viewer input), CREDIT (u32 flow-control credit), RESIZE (u16 cols,rows), FOCUS (1 byte), FACTS (Display JSON) and CLOSE per channel; channel-0 calls run concurrently so slow calls never block typing.
- CAT-3116 reply overflow disconnect: A framed client that stops reading until its replies exceed MAX_CONTROL is disconnected with a stderr note.
- CAT-3117 machine.exec ends with its caller: A plain connection running machine.exec watches the socket; if the caller closes, the exec is aborted; framed callers can send $/cancelRequest {id}; execs also end when the connection drops.
- CAT-3119 terminal.attach needs framed: terminal.attach on a plain connection returns kind needs_framed with hint to send hello framed:true or use `hc attach`.
- CAT-3141 screen exact/inexact: screen is exact, or inexact after a core crash when older history may be missing.
- CAT-3142 printed / full_screen: printed counts newlines output; more than the history holds means reads are incomplete; full_screen marks alt-screen apps whose history cannot be scrolled back after exit.
- CAT-3146 retention policy: Finished terminals are pruned after 24 h (HC_RETAIN_MS overrides), max 500 finished (oldest first); a finished child with a live parent is kept until the parent has seen it, then a day after.
- CAT-3150 Core::attach: Adds a viewer, opens a new channel, queues the first paint (screen plus history), then every live byte; errors finished (with hint hc read) when no screen, unavailable when lost.
- CAT-3151 size leadership: The most recently active non-observer viewer sets terminal size and display facts; with no typing viewer the terminal is headless at config headless size (default 200x120); resize emits a `size` event and tells the holder.
- CAT-3153 output pipeline: Relay to screen and viewers, feeds output_watch waiters, replies to holder, parses OSC 7501 and title; viewers that overflow get a full repaint (first_paint) instead of replay; emits title events.
- CAT-3156 stitch pauses viewers: While a stitched read scrolls an app, viewers get no frames and wait watchers get nothing; one repaint follows.
- CAT-3168 MAX_PAYLOAD: A frame payload is capped at 16 MiB
- CAT-3170 CREDIT frame kind (1): u32 LE count of bytes consumed; the sender may send that many more
- CAT-3173 WINDOW initial credit: Each stream starts with 256 KiB of credit before any acknowledgement
- CAT-3174 MAX_PENDING: At most 4 MiB is kept for a viewer that stopped reading; past that it gets a repaint
- CAT-3175 MAX_CONTROL: At most 64 MiB of replies is kept for a non-reading client; past that it is dropped
- CAT-3176 EOF mid-header is clean end: UnexpectedEof while reading a header is Ok(None), not an error
- CAT-3179 Conn.overflowed notify: Fires when the connection fell past MAX_CONTROL and must end
- CAT-3182 Outbox control overflow: Past MAX_CONTROL, everything is dropped and nothing more is taken or sent
- CAT-3184 Outbox::data backpressure: Returns false and clears the backlog past MAX_PENDING so the caller replaces it with a repaint

### herdr-core / src/api

- CAT-3192 finished history cap: History reads of finished terminals or stitched full-screen reads are capped at 1000 lines.
- CAT-3194 Call context: A call carries the core plus an optional framed connection or a plain subscription slot; framed-only methods fail on plain connections.
- CAT-3201 remote list timeout: Remote machines are asked in parallel with a 3 s timeout; a slow or failed machine is simply omitted from terminal.list (its state appears only in machines).
- CAT-3206 terminal.read: Returns screen plus `lines` of history as text with `complete`, `how` (screen, history, stitched) and `why` fields; live or finished.
- CAT-3207 alt-screen read stitching: For an alternate-screen app with lines>0 the core scrolls to stitch history; if that fails it returns only the visible screen with complete false and why working when the program is working.
- CAT-3208 terminal.attach: Opens a raw stream to a live terminal on a framed connection (needs hello framed); loss ends the stream even when kept.
- CAT-3227 plain-mode subscription: On a non-framed connection events.subscribe stores a PlainSub in the connection slot and the stream continues as newline JSON on that same socket; no heartbeat task is started for it.
- CAT-3237 template ready_when_quiet: Template flag makes readiness be judged by output quiet rather than status report.
- CAT-3241 alt-screen output read: After a waited run, a full-screen (alt screen) app is read with lines=0 (screen only), else FINISHED_LINES of history.
- CAT-3242 run output tail 50,000 bytes: tail() keeps at most 50,000 bytes of whole lines from the end and prefixes a `[hc] earlier output cut: hc read <addr> --lines N` pointer.
- CAT-3245 remote caller has no folder here: If caller address contains `/` (another machine) cwd falls back to home via exec::folder(.., from_afar).
- CAT-3253 TERM_PROGRAM masquerades as ghostty: If TERM_PROGRAM is unset or "herdr" it becomes "ghostty" and version is dropped.
- CAT-3262 busy = unreported or working: A child counts busy if live and either has not reported status yet or state is "working".
- CAT-3265 unreachable machine silently omitted: Failed side results are dropped via `continue`, so a lost machine is not reported in the merged result.
- CAT-3268 framed mode switch: HelloParams.framed switches the connection to framed mode after the reply.
- CAT-3277 --bg / wait default: CLI waits unless --bg; API wait defaults false.
- CAT-3278 caller identity field: caller (HC_TERMINAL_ID) filled by hc, not the user; drives parent defaults and seen-tracking.
- CAT-3281 terminal.keep: Toggle keep; existing streams end with loss reason, reattach after `restarted`.
- CAT-3283 full-screen apps not scrolled while working: Read of an alt-screen app returns only the screen with why="working"; read again after it stops.
- CAT-3285 attach channel frames: DATA keys, RESIZE, FOCUS, FACTS, CREDIT, CLOSE frames control the attach channel (credit flow control).
- CAT-3287 subscribe seq and missed snapshot: Events after seq follow; after a `missed` snapshot ignore events with seq not above the snapshot.
- CAT-3288 plain-mode subscription: In plain mode the connection carries only notifications after the reply; framed mode uses a credit channel with JSON lines.
- CAT-3293 started null for non-reporting programs: No way to tell if input took effect.
- CAT-3302 machine rename/list/params: Rename breaks old addresses; MachineListResult lists views.

### herdr-core / src/cli

- CAT-3309 API-only methods: hello, doc.get and doc.set have no CLI command.
- CAT-3317 shell-line heuristic: A single argv string containing shell characters is treated as a shell line.
- CAT-3318 template trailing flags: For templates, hc flags after the task text are parsed as hc flags.
- CAT-3319 hc read output: Read prints plain text even when piped; JSON only with --json; appends incomplete markers.
- CAT-3340 auto-install hc on remote when missing/incompatible: On `hc_missing` or `incompatible` errors, copies this hc there (prompts `[Y/n]` unless `--install`), then retries `machine.add`.
- CAT-3343 login requires a terminal: Non-TTY returns `usage` "logging in needs a terminal".
- CAT-3346 machine update runs client-side install, not an RPC: `machines::install` is called directly from the CLI using the machine's recorded session.
- CAT-3351 done is not acknowledged: Comment: "Done stays done after you looked (hc can't tell)"; done ranks with idle.
- CAT-3358 wait timeout is not terminal: `timeout` and `running` mean still running, so the caller must wait again.
- CAT-3360 Windows needs SSH keys before login: On Windows, `needs_login` tells you to set up SSH keys first (`cfg!(windows)`).
- CAT-3363 exec output truncation: If `truncated`, notes the first 8 MB of stdout and 1 MB of stderr were kept.
- CAT-3364 exec_out terminates the process: Return type `!`; calls `process::exit`.

### herdr-core / src/platform

- CAT-3376 Windows signal mapping: On Windows only INT (Ctrl+C byte) is graceful; any other signal and hang_up terminate the whole job.
- CAT-3378 No systemd user manager fallback: Without a manager (or systemd-run) the core is started the plain way and ends with whatever started it; only a stderr warning is printed.
- CAT-3385 macOS watch failure is silent: If notify registration fails the core logs to stderr and runs without shutdown detection.
- CAT-3387 Windows autostart refusal: Implicit (non-explicit) autostart over SSH is refused with RpcError code unavailable if an elevated core would block a desktop session for the same user; hint: open Herdr or run hc server start in a desktop terminal.
- CAT-3388 Windows status does not start core: status_may_start_core is false on Windows (true on Unix).
- CAT-3392 MAX_SOCKET_PATH: Longest Unix socket path is sun_path-1 (macOS 103, Linux 107); Windows pipe names up to 256.
- CAT-3409 Windows Stream over overlapped named pipe: Connection is a cloneable Arc pipe in overlapped mode so reads and writes from different threads proceed concurrently; shutdown cancels IO and disconnects (cannot half-close); set_read_timeout is a no-op.
- CAT-3410 Windows pipe ACL: Pipe SDDL grants only SYSTEM and the current user plus a mandatory integrity label (HI if elevated else ME) so lower-integrity processes cannot drive it; remote clients rejected.
- CAT-3412 Windows spawn_detached: Starts without console, breaking away from the launching job, handle list restricted to NUL and log so ssh pipes are not inherited; if ssh job kills on close and refuses breakaway it errors.
- CAT-3413 Windows termination never fires: No SIGTERM on Windows; termination() is pending forever, planned restarts come through the API.
- CAT-3415 Windows command resolution: argv[0] resolved on env PATH with PATHEXT (default .COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD); .cmd/.bat go through cmd.exe; error NotFound if missing.
- CAT-3416 batch_line quoting: Batch arguments quoted with quote doubling and % defused as %%cd:~, so a prompt is one literal argument; args with CR/LF/NUL rejected as InvalidInput.

### herdr-core / src/remote

- CAT-3424 line supervision: Core dials each added machine over ssh stdio with hello {framed, core, calls_you}, redials immediately after a drop, backoff 250 ms doubling up to HC_RECONNECT_MS (30 s); checks the remote core id matches.
- CAT-3429 machine_timeout / wait_timeout: Remote deadline = config machine_timeout plus, for waits, the requested timeout (default config wait_timeout else 180 s, max 86400); machine.exec clamps to 600 s plus 5 s.
- CAT-3431 remote attach relay: Viewer frames are forwarded to the remote channel; while the line is down typing is lost, not queued; viewers get a "[line to X lost; reconnecting...]" notice in the data stream and are reattached with resumed:true.

### herdr-core / src/runtime

- CAT-3445 save / save_soon: Registry saved atomically; frequent changes saved within SAVE_SOON=2 s (one write per burst); a changed status word is saved at once.
- CAT-3447 screen restore: After a planned handover screens restore exactly from snapshot; after a crash the screen is rebuilt from the holder tail (inexact), a resize nudge asks full-screen programs to repaint, and at most one turn ending while down is counted.
- CAT-3451 server stop ends all programs: server.stop marks stopping, kills every live terminal (reason server_stop), waits for execs and sweeps; only server.restart/SIGTERM preserves programs.
- CAT-3469 Unix-only holder tests and socket pair: Holder tests are `#[cfg(unix)]` and use `UnixStream`. Windows holder behavior is not covered here.

### herdr-core / tests

- CAT-3482 missed event after machine reconnect; doc.set/doc.get take `on`: doc ops route to a machine via `on`; after a line drop the subscriber gets `missed` with seq and must refetch.
- CAT-3488 Client that stops reading replies is disconnected: Core hangs up on a connection whose unread replies exceed a cap (~64 MB) rather than buffering.
- CAT-3503 Pending recovery: input/attach refused kind unavailable: terminal.send/keys/interrupt/attach return unavailable "lost, waiting for its new shell"; kill still wins.
- CAT-3504 spawn_pending reason when holder frozen at run timeout: Record stays live with null pid and reason spawn_pending; late spawn stays addressable.
- CAT-3510 hello {framed:true} switches to framed mode (channel, kind, payload): wire::encode(channel, DATA, json); channel 0 carries RPC.
- CAT-3521 Core restart cuts waits with message "restarted": Command waiting during restart errors saying restarted; program keeps running.
- CAT-3523 Attach viewer: first paint then live bytes; queries answered by core: DA1 and OSC 11 answered once by the core using viewer display.bg; headless default bg 2828/2c2c/3434.
- CAT-3524 Size follows last active typing viewer; headless 200x120; observe:true: RESIZE/FOCUS frames; observers never lead.
- CAT-3525 Flow control: CREDIT frames and wire::WINDOW: Stalled viewer receives no more than credit, own connection still answers, catches up via repaint.
- CAT-3526 Close frame carries exit_code; attach errors finished / needs_framed: plain connection attach -> needs_framed.
- CAT-3535 missed + snapshot, heartbeat (HC_HEARTBEAT_MS), PLAIN_QUEUE: Slow subscriber gets missed with terminals snapshot after queue overflow.
- CAT-3546 <hc>...</hc> notes typed into parent for blocked/error/exited child: Notes only for unseen news, never into blocked parent or non-agent; --no-notify; config notes=false turns off.
- CAT-3547 Messages between agents tagged <hc from="t1 name">: Person sends untouched; shell gets plain.
- CAT-3555 Frozen machine never freezes hc: machine_timeout config; unavailable; state unreachable.
- CAT-3556 Addresses machine/tN: Remote terminals show as rohan/t1; denied for non-parents.
- CAT-3557 Viewer rides out dropped line; no size takeover: Stream stays open; "lost" shown.
- CAT-3560 HC_SOCKET / HC_SESSION; long names rejected: Socket path length "too long".
- CAT-3564 read --lines on full-screen app: how stitched/screen, complete, why: Scrolls app via mouse wheel to reconstruct history; any doubt returns plain screen incomplete; why working.
- CAT-3582 Windows' built-in ConPTY swallows the core's answers: Answers reach the program only with the bundled conpty.dll (scripts\fetch-conpty.ps1); the test asserts the DLL is present.
- CAT-3587 Refuse implicit start that would die at ssh logout: With SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT and no core, start is refused (or started headless) with message mentioning `desktop session` or log out and hint `open Herdr on that Windows machine`; no core left behind.
- CAT-3589 Core inside a kill-on-close job object is refused: If the job kills on close and cannot be left, ending the session would end every terminal, so start is refused.
- CAT-3594 One connection per CLI call (one call per command): Every harness call spawns a fresh CLI process; `out()` waits for stdout close so a core started by the CLI must not inherit the pipe.
- CAT-3602 Reply read is blind to interleaved events: `Conn::call` reads exactly the next line as the reply with no id matching; an event arriving first would be mistaken for the reply.
- CAT-3607 Remote login needs interactive OTP: `otp-` targets require a prior login (`<target> exit` prompts for a verification code), after which ssh master lets later calls in.
- CAT-3615 Client must run its own VT emulator: To know screen contents from the attach stream a client needs a terminal emulator (1 MiB scrollback in test).
- CAT-3616 Credit-based flow control: A well-behaved viewer returns CREDIT equal to payload length after each DATA; `credit` flag lets tests withhold it.
- CAT-3619 Out-of-order frames must be stashed: While waiting for an RPC reply, stream frames for other channels arrive and must be buffered by the client.
- CAT-3624 Plain connection: 10 s read timeout, one connection per Conn: `connect` opens a fresh Unix stream with 10 s read timeout; test usage opens separate connections per purpose.

### herdr-core / docs

- CAT-3649 hc server: Starts, stops, inspects, or restarts core.
- CAT-3665 Interactive machine credentials: SSH passwords, codes, and host-key prompts require a person at a terminal.
- CAT-3667 Temporary machine marker: `--temp` only helps clients display short-lived machines separately; it does not remove them.
- CAT-3668 hc machine login: Reconnects after credentials are needed; Windows requires SSH keys first.
- CAT-3669 Remote stdout purity: Remote login must print no extra text to stdout because the connection is a byte protocol.
- CAT-3672 API authority: Any API client can run commands, read/change files, and control terminals with core account access.
- CAT-3673 Templates are not isolation: Templates are shell commands and opening instructions, not isolation rules.
- CAT-3674 Blocked status is not access control: Blocked can prevent normal send but is not a security boundary against another client.
- CAT-3675 Session isolation boundary: `HC_SESSION` selects separate core/state, but same-account processes can select the same session; config/templates are shared.
- CAT-3678 Core state contents: State stores terminal records, screen/history, machine connections, peers, API documents, and logs; it is unencrypted and may contain secrets.
- CAT-3679 Release integrity: Updates verify archive SHA-256 against HTTPS manifest, but manifest has no independent signature.
- CAT-3680 Windows release signing: Windows signing is conditional; unsigned builds may be published when profile is unset.
- CAT-3681 Local build update trust: `hc update --from` installs a local build; compatibility checks do not review its code.
- CAT-3683 Template readiness: By default core waits for first status report; after 30 seconds without one, it leaves screen alone.
- CAT-3684 Quiet readiness: `ready: quiet` waits for output to settle but does not prove readiness or set agent status.
- CAT-3685 hc send conditions: `--if` sends only when status exactly matches idle or working; `--force` types even if blocked; `--wait` waits for started turn.
- CAT-3693 Paid real-agent smoke: Real-agent smokes cost money and require asking before running.
- CAT-3696 Supported release: Only the latest release is supported; response deadline is not fixed.
- CAT-3697 hc update version semantics: `--version` means at least that version; `--force` permits older or another protocol generation.

### herdr-core / schema

- CAT-3706 Windows input encoding: Core does not encode keys; viewers honoring 9001 must send key events in that format.
- CAT-3713 Recovery unavailable window: During recovery, send/keys/interrupt/attach return unavailable until restarted event.
- CAT-3714 Spawn-pending claim: Timed-out initial spawn remains claimed; input/attach unavailable until holder answers; explicit kill cancels it.
- CAT-3719 Document API-only: Document methods have no CLI verb.
- CAT-3721 Document subscription recovery: Subscribe before reading; refetch after reconnect, missed notification, or remote reconnect because document snapshots/replay are absent.
- CAT-3723 Windows signal reporting: Windows reports no signals, so signal-based `signaled` recovery does not fire there.
- CAT-3734 terminal.read: Required terminal, optional caller/history lines; returns screen and history text plus completeness and read method.
- CAT-3738 terminal.keys: Required terminal and key names; optional caller; encodes named keys for program keyboard modes.
- CAT-3751 machine.rename: Required current and new names; changes only this core's name for the machine; old addresses stop working.
- CAT-3752 machine.rm: Required machine name; forgets machine while its terminals keep running there.
- CAT-3760 read completeness: `terminal.read` may return incomplete text; a working full-screen application is not scrolled, so retry after it stops.
- CAT-3762 guarded send: Send waits for about three seconds of human inactivity, holds concurrent human keys, and refuses blocked programs unless forced.
- CAT-3764 execution output bounds: Exec captures first 8 MB stdout and first 1 MB stderr as base64 and reports truncation and timeout.
- CAT-3769 API socket interaction: `events.subscribe` result may use a framed event channel; plain mode turns the connection into notifications only.

### herdr-core / SKILL

- CAT-3771 Agent skill bootstrap: When inside hc use hc; otherwise ask user once whether to use hc; run `hc --skill` before use.
- CAT-3774 First task delivery: Put first task in `run`; if first_message.sent is false, inspect screen and resolve readiness before sending.
- CAT-3775 Avoid blind resend: After failed send, read first because message may already have arrived.
- CAT-3778 Wait check-in: Wait timeout (default 180s) is a check-in, not failure; wait can return before all children finish.
- CAT-3781 Terminal cleanup: Kill then remove only terminals you started; `hc ls` includes other user work.
- CAT-3782 Core restart caution: Never stop or restart user's core unless asked because it affects every terminal.
- CAT-3783 Codex no-daemon: Codex must run with `--no-daemon`, including templates, or commands execute outside hc.
- CAT-3784 Foreground sampling: Jobs shorter than foreground sampling interval may not be observed.
- CAT-3786 Blocked and error handling: On blocked, read screen and ask user; do not bypass permission with force. On error, read why before sending or killing.

## Protocols

### herdr socket API

- Transport: newline-delimited JSON; a request is `{id, method, params}` with a client-chosen string id (CAT-001 `herdr/src/api/schema.rs:37`); the client writes one JSON line and reads one line (CAT-061 `herdr/src/api/client.rs:185`).
- One request per connection: ordinary methods read one line, answer and close (CAT-079 `herdr/src/api/server.rs:328`); the bundled ApiClient connects, writes, reads and drops the stream per call (CAT-060 `herdr/src/api/client.rs:55`).
